egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:9:A **test** describes a situation to put an agent in, and names the **personas** who should call about it. Every test has one home inside its **project**: a **test suite**, the named container for tests normally run and reviewed together. Executing one complete suite is a **run**; each test executed once inside it is a **simulation**, which produces a **transcript**, an **outcome**, and **metrics**. **Graders** read those and return verdicts.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:16:- **project** — a product area inside it: *Outbound*, *Support*. **A permission scope and a query filter — never a wall.** A project isolates nothing; it labels rows so a permission can name a subset and a query can filter to one. Two projects in the same organization are always queryable together. **Tests, personas and graders all belong to a project**, not to an agent. A test has no agent assignment or applicability list, so the same complete suite can run against any selected agent and the results stay comparable. That comparison is the whole point of testing prompt variants, and it is impossible if each agent owns its own copy. Because the project owns nothing, an asset is never *trapped* in one — the failure that forced Humanloop to rebuild its datasets and graders as new object types. See [What is scoped to a project, and what stays at the organization](.scratch/first-simulation-path/issues/17-project-versus-organization-scoping.md).
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:26:**agent platform** — the product or framework that runs or exposes an agent, such as Retell, Vapi, LiveKit Agents or Pipecat. An agent platform can offer several connections to the same agent; it is not itself the way egma reaches that agent. A connection can also be platform-agnostic, so its platform may be unknown. Do not call it a runtime: `simulator` is egma's execution system, and earlier records use runtime only for that system. Added 2026-08-09 during the self-hosted phone onboarding grilling; clarified 2026-08-19 during the production-monitoring grilling.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:30:**connection** — how egma's simulator reaches an agent. **Each connection belongs to one agent, and an agent can have many connections.** A LiveKit agent can be reached through its LiveKit room or through a generic phone number; the platform and the connection are separate facts. A connection describes simulation reach. It does not describe how egma receives records of real production conversations.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:58:**persona** — the synthetic person who calls the agent. Who they are: manner, patience, accent, background noise, and how they behave under friction. A first-class, reusable, versioned entity. A persona is either **Egma-provided** and shared read-only, or **Custom** and owned by one project.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:60:**persona version** — one immutable, executable form of a persona. It owns the caller's traits and the complete model selection used to bring that caller to life: LLM provider and model, STT provider and model, and TTS provider, model, voice ID, and speed. The technical voice has no second home in traits or platform settings. Editing any of these facts creates a new persona version.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:62:A persona says nothing about *what* the caller wants — that's the test's scenario. The same persona calls about many different things.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:64:Every project carries one active **default persona** — a project choice, not a persona type. A new project points at Egma's shared default persona. A project may point at any active Egma-provided or Custom persona available to it instead. A default cannot be archived until the project pointer moves. A test created naming no callers receives this pointer, so authoring a first test never waits on authoring a caller.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:68:> Renamed from `digital human` on 2026-08-05 (public issue #8). `digital human` was originally chosen over `persona` for saying plainly that the caller is synthetic — accepting that users arriving from other tools would say "persona" and need correcting. They did say it, and the correcting bought nothing: `persona` is the voice industry's near-unanimous term, and now it is egma's. Also considered and still not chosen: `simulant`, `virtual human`, `synthetic user`, `phantom`, `surrogate`.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:75:- **personas** — an array. One to start; several when a scenario should be checked against several kinds of caller. Three personas on a test means running it produces three simulations.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:85:**mock tool** — a project-owned stand-in for one of the agent's tools: the tool's name, and the answer egma serves when the agent calls it during a simulation. The answer may be an error — that is how a test forces the failure branch — and may carry a delay, so a mocked backend takes as long as the real one would. **Matching is by tool name, strictly: one answer per tool.** A mock tool never reads a call's arguments; wrong arguments are caught by grading, not matching, because the arguments are on the record either way. Chosen over `tool mock` because it is the word users arrive with (Cekura, Vapi) — the persona lesson, applied the cheap way this time. Added 2026-08-09, mock-tools grilling.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:97:**A run pins the versions it executed against** through its evidence records, not through a versioned suite. Each simulation pins its exact test and persona versions, and the run's grading plan pins its exact grader versions. Editing any of them cannot rewrite what last week's result meant. **Authored things are never overwritten**: an edit creates a new version and the old one remains. Mock tools are the single exception — unversioned by decision, and held to one world per run by snapshot rather than by version, for the reasons the Mock tools section gives. The run row itself keeps the stable suite ID and no second pinned-test list. See [ADR-0013](docs/adr/0013-test-suites-are-containers.md) and [The Postgres control-plane schema](.scratch/first-simulation-path/issues/08-postgres-control-plane-schema.md).
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:101:A run produces one simulation per test per persona. Running the same test twice produces two simulations — there is no separate word for a repeat.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:105:**simulator** — the component that executes a simulation: it brings the persona to life, holds the conversation with the agent over a connection, and emits the transcript, outcome, metrics and spans. It runs inside egma's own deployment, hosted or self-hosted — never anywhere else. Earlier records call it *the runtime* or *the simulation runtime*; `simulator` is the canonical name, adopted 2026-08-03 when the simulator effort began.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:123:**metric** — something **measured**, not judged: duration, turn count, latency percentiles, interruption count, tool-call count, cost. **Derived from the trace's spans by one shared measure module** — the same computation serves the metrics display and the graders, for simulations and production traces alike, so the number on screen and the number judged can never disagree. (Previously *emitted by the runtime*; re-homed to spans 2026-08-14, grader-redesign grilling — the simulator's duty is emitting honest span timings.) Never an entity, never attached to a test.
egma-planning/CONTEXT.md:149:**predefined grader** — a library entry egma owns and ships. v0 ships two: **expected_behaviors** (`llm_as_judge`) and **latency** (`code`). Replaces *built-in grader*, 2026-08-14 — `predefined` is the word users arrive with (Cekura), the persona lesson applied the cheap way again.

Added 2026-08-06 after the walking-skeleton code review hit the contradiction. egma-planning/.scratch/simulation-recordings/spec.md:49:- **Naming an object-storage endpoint is what selects it.** Absent, the filesystem implementation stands. egma-planning/.scratch/simulation-recordings/spec.md:52:- **One file, written when the conversation ends.** Two alternatives were considered and declined: streaming to scratch storage during the call, and chunked upload. egma-planning/.scratch/simulation-recordings/spec.md:84:*Memory peaks at roughly six times the audio.* Building the file copies both tracks, allocates an interleaved buffer, converts it, writes it into a memory buffer, and copies it out again. On the narrow band a telephone carries — the path actually run today — a full-length call is about ten megabytes and peaks near sixty, which is nothing. On the wide band a browser connection carries, the same call is about sixty megabytes and peaks near three hundred, and a simulator conducts several at once. Deferred by the founder with the number known. The fix is contained to the file that builds the recording and does not touch this effort's seams.
egma-planning/.scratch/simulation-recordings/spec.md:86:**A recording that fails to upload is silent, and looks exactly like a call that never connected.** Found during ticket 01's review and left standing, with the shape of it written down here rather than discovered by a customer. The simulator builds the recording, offers it to the store, and — if the store refuses or cannot be reached — logs the refusal and reports the simulation with no audio block at all. The conversation, the transcript and the ending are all reported correctly; what is lost is the reference *and* the measured band, which is the one fact a reader would need to tell "the upload failed" from "there was never any audio". A voice simulation whose call never connected reports the same absence, and the product is about to show both of them the same way: no player. So a deployment with a wrong credential, a full bucket, or a store on the wrong address loses every recording and looks, from every surface, like a platform working correctly. It is visible only in the simulator's container log.
egma-planning/.scratch/simulation-recordings/spec.md:90:**Two dependency trees arrive.** The simulator gains an object-storage client, wrapped the way its existing filesystem writes are wrapped so a network call never stalls another simulation. The control plane — which carries very few runtime dependencies by design — gains the ability to sign a link. Signing one kind of read request by hand is small and would avoid the tree; it is also security-adjacent code nobody should write twice. The choice is named in the ticket that builds it, to be made with the trade in view rather than by default.

egma-planning/.scratch/first-simulation-path/map.md:19:**Platforms split two ways, and the split predicts what data we can get.** **Customer-run** (LiveKit, Pipecat — and egma's own persona, which runs on Pipecat) execute on the customer's machines and already emit OpenTelemetry natively, so egma writes no transport for them. **Vendor-run** (Retell, Vapi, ElevenLabs) run on the vendor's infrastructure; the customer connects a platform API key, and egma imports the agent config and pulls call data back through it — nothing of ours runs inside their agent, so we get what their API chooses to give and nothing more. Two rules bind every adapter: **keep the vendor's payload verbatim** alongside anything derived from it, and **never invent a span we did not observe** — a missing span is honest, a fabricated one poisons every cross-platform comparison. **Retell specifically:** per-turn *content* is available (per-utterance transcript with word-level timings, tool calls pinned to the triggering word); per-turn *latency* is not (only p50–p99 distributions plus a raw array with nothing tying a value to an utterance). On the wide band a browser connection carries, the same call is about sixty megabytes and peaks near three hundred, and a simulator conducts several at once. egma-planning/.scratch/simulation-recordings/spec.md:86:**A recording that fails to upload is silent, and looks exactly like a call that never connected.** Found during ticket 01's review and left standing, with the shape of it written down here rather than discovered by a customer. The conversation, the transcript and the ending are all reported correctly; what is lost is the reference *and* the measured band, which is the one fact a reader would need to tell "the upload failed" from "there was never any audio". A voice simulation whose call never connected reports the same absence, and the product is about to show both of them the same way: no player. 1	"""Pipeline assembly: what one simulation is conducted through.
     2	
     3	One pipeline is built from one claimed spec and torn down when the
     4	exchange is over, so nothing from one simulation can reach the next. What
     5	the spec selects is only which legs are in it: a chat simulation is the
     6	plug and the persona brain, and a voice simulation is the same plug and
     7	the same brain with speech legs between them. The brain is one component
     8	for every modality, forever — it never learns which of these it is in.
     9	
    10	**Who conducts is what a spec selects here, and there are two answers.**
    11	A chat simulation is walked a turn at a time by :mod:`egma_simulator.walk`.
    12	A voice simulation is conducted by :mod:`egma_simulator.conductor` — a
    13	real Pipecat pipeline on a full-duplex transport, with the voice activity
    14	detector and the turn model deciding where turns fall instead of a loop.
    15	There is no third answer and no byte adapter between them: every voice
    16	connection gives the conductor one Pipecat transport, whether it is a
    17	local fixture, a phone call, or a room.
    18	
    19	Constructing is validation and nothing else, which is what makes a spec
    20	that cannot be conducted an honest failure before anything is dialled.
    21	"""
    22	
    23	from __future__ import annotations
    24	
    25	import logging
    26	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    27	
    28	from .blob import BlobStore
    29	from .conductor import DEFAULT_CONDUCT, ConductParameters, VoiceConductor
    30	from .config import MediaSettings
    31	from .mock_tools import ExchangedToolCall, MockToolSeam
    32	from .plugs import ConnectionPlug, PlugError, VoiceConnection, plug_for
    33	from .recording import RECORDING_NAME
    34	from .spec import SimulationSpec
    35	from .speech import SpeechProviders, voice_from_models
    36	
    37	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    38	
    39	
    40	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    41	class Assembled:
    42	    """One simulation's pipeline: who conducts it, and what it recorded.
    43	
    44	    Exactly one of the two is filled in. ``plug`` is what the walk drives,
    45	    which is a chat platform and only ever that. ``conductor`` is the
    46	    voice conductor, which owns the plug's Pipecat transport.
    47	    """
    48	
    49	    plug: ConnectionPlug | None = None
    50	    """Text in, text out — the walk's whole view of a platform."""
    51	
    52	    conductor: VoiceConductor | None = None
    53	    """The Pipecat pipeline conducting a full-duplex voice simulation."""
    54	
    55	    mock_tools: MockToolSeam = field(default_factory=MockToolSeam)
    56	    """egma's side of the mock-tool exchange, for whichever plug can offer
    57	    it. Always here and never ``None``, because whether egma really stood
    58	    in the agent's tool path is the seam's own answer to give — a plug
    59	    that cannot offer it simply never says it is standing ready, and the
    60	    record then claims nothing about tools."""
    61	
    62	    @property
    63	    def audio(self) -> dict | None:
    64	        """The contract's audio block once the exchange is over, else ``None``."""
    65	        measured = None if self.conductor is None else self.conductor.audio
    66	        return None if measured is None else measured.as_report()
    67	
    68	    @property
    69	    def mock_tool_coverage(self) -> dict | None:
    70	        """The contract's coverage stamp, or ``None`` where nothing is claimed."""
    71	        return self.mock_tools.coverage()
    72	
    73	    def tool_calls(self) -> list[ExchangedToolCall]:
    74	        """Every mock-tool call since this was last asked, and then none."""
    75	        return self.mock_tools.exchanged()
    76	
    77	
    78	def assemble(
    79	    spec: SimulationSpec,
    80	    *,
    81	    blobs: BlobStore,
    82	    speech: SpeechProviders,
    83	    media: MediaSettings | None = None,
    84	    parameters: ConductParameters | None = None,
    85	) -> Assembled:
    86	    """Build one simulation's pipeline from its spec.
    87	
    88	    Constructing is validation and nothing else — no platform is dialled
    89	    and no pipeline is started until the exchange opens — so a spec that
    90	    cannot be conducted fails here, honestly, before anything happens.
    91	
    92	    ``speech`` is the pinned persona version's direct STT and TTS selection.
    93	    It is required even for chat, where no speech legs are built, so callers
    94	    cannot grow a second fallback assembly path.
    95	
    96	    ``media`` is the same for the telephone network — this container's
    97	    bridge with the platform's own carrier already laid over it, resolved
    98	    once by whoever built these arguments and handed whole to the plug.
    99	    ``None`` is a deployment that places no calls, and a spec that then
   100	    names a phone number is refused by the plug with a sentence saying so.
   101	    """
   102	    factory = plug_for(spec.connection_type)
   103	    if factory is None:
   104	        raise PlugError(
   105	            f"no adapter for connection type {spec.connection_type!r}"
   106	        )
   107	    # Built for every simulation, and handed to every plug: which of them
   108	    # can put egma in front of the agent's tools is the plug's own answer,
   109	    # not a list kept here of the ones that can. A plug that cannot takes
   110	    # it and drops it, and the seam then says there is nothing to claim.
   111	    mock_tools = MockToolSeam(spec.mock_tools)
   112	    plug = factory(
   113	        modality=spec.modality,
   114	        access_variant=spec.access_variant,
   115	        config=spec.connection_config,
   116	        credentials=spec.credentials,
   117	        simulation_id=spec.simulation_id,
   118	        mock_tools=mock_tools,
   119	        media=media,
   120	    )
   121	    if spec.modality != "voice":
   122	        return Assembled(plug=plug, mock_tools=mock_tools)
   123	
   124	    if not isinstance(plug, VoiceConnection):
   125	        # Unreachable through the shipped registry, and kept because the
   126	        # alternative is a voice simulation with nobody to conduct it,
   127	        # discovered somewhere far away from the plug that was wrong.
   128	        raise PlugError(
   129	            f"the adapter for connection type {spec.connection_type!r} speaks "
   130	            "voice but is not a Pipecat voice connection, so nothing can conduct it"
   131	        )
   132	    return Assembled(
   133	        conductor=VoiceConductor(
   134	            connection=plug,
   135	            voice=voice_from_models(spec.models),
   136	            speech=speech,
   137	            blobs=blobs,
   138	            recording_key=f"{spec.simulation_id}/{RECORDING_NAME}",
   139	            parameters=parameters or DEFAULT_CONDUCT,
   140	        ),
   141	        mock_tools=mock_tools,
   142	    )

1	"""The persona brain: one component, shared by every modality forever.
     2	
     3	It composes the persona's authored human traits and the test's scenario into a
     4	system prompt, takes turns — the transcript's ``human`` side — and decides
     5	when the exchange is concluded. What it does not know is deliberate: it
     6	never sees a platform (that is the plug's business) and never produces its
     7	own words (that is the model client's), so the same brain conducts a chat
     8	today and speaks through voice legs when those arrive.
     9	
    10	Role mapping is from the persona's own seat at the table: the persona is
    11	the ``assistant`` the model plays, and the agent under test is the
    12	``user`` it is answering.
    13	"""
    14	
    15	from __future__ import annotations
    16	
    17	import json
    18	from collections.abc import Sequence
    19	from dataclasses import dataclass
    20	from typing import Any
    21	
    22	from .model import CONCLUDE_MARKER, ModelClient, PersonaReply
    23	
    24	OPENING_NUDGE = (
    25	    "(The conversation is open and the agent is listening. Speak your first turn.)"
    26	)
    27	"""Stands in for the silence when the persona goes first: chat-shaped
    28	models answer a user message, and an empty history has none to answer."""
    29	
    30	_PROMPT_FRAME = """\
    31	You are playing a person in a live conversation with a customer service \
    32	agent. You are the person; the agent is who you are talking to.
    33	
    34	Who you are, exactly as authored:
    35	
    36	{traits}
    37	
    38	Why you are here today:
    39	
    40	{scenario}
    41	
    42	How to conduct yourself:
    43	- Stay in character as this person for the whole exchange. Never mention \
    44	being simulated, tested, or an AI.
    45	- Speak one conversational turn at a time, in plain spoken words — no \
    46	lists, no headings, no stage directions.
    47	- Pursue what you came for until it is concluded to your satisfaction, \
    48	and let your persona decide how patiently.
    49	- When your goal is concluded and nothing further is needed, say a brief \
    50	goodbye and end your reply with {marker}.
    51	"""
    52	
    53	
    54	def compose_system_prompt(traits: dict[str, Any], scenario_instructions: str) -> str:
    55	    """Human traits and scenario, composed into the persona's instructions.
    56	
    57	    Contract v3 admits the complete human-traits value and excludes technical
    58	    voice. Render that complete value so every authored human fact reaches the
    59	    model, without a model or deployment fallback.
    60	    """
    61	    return _PROMPT_FRAME.format(
    62	        traits=json.dumps(traits, indent=2, sort_keys=True),
    63	        scenario=scenario_instructions,
    64	        marker=CONCLUDE_MARKER,
    65	    )
    66	
    67	
    68	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    69	class Turn:
    70	    """One transcript turn: who spoke (``human`` or ``agent``), and what."""
    71	
    72	    speaker: str
    73	    text: str
    74	
    75	
    76	def messages_for(system_prompt: str, history: Sequence[Turn]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    77	    """The conversation so far, in chat shape, from the persona's seat."""
    78	    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}]
    79	    for turn in history:
    80	        role = "assistant" if turn.speaker == "human" else "user"
    81	        messages.append({"role": role, "content": turn.text})
    82	    if not history:
    83	        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": OPENING_NUDGE})
    84	    return messages
    85	
    86	
    87	class Persona:
    88	    """The synthetic person on the human side of the transcript."""
    89	
    90	    def __init__(
    91	        self,
    92	        *,
    93	        traits: dict[str, Any],
    94	        scenario_instructions: str,
    95	        model: ModelClient,
    96	    ) -> None:
    97	        self._system_prompt = compose_system_prompt(traits, scenario_instructions)
    98	        self._model = model
    99	
   100	    @property
   101	    def model_name(self) -> str:
   102	        """The provider model label Pipecat records on its native span."""
   103	        return self._model.model_name
   104	
   105	    def messages(self, history: Sequence[Turn]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
   106	        """The exact provider input for this point in the conversation."""
   107	        return messages_for(self._system_prompt, history)
   108	
   109	    async def reply_to(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply:
   110	        """Ask the configured model without changing its provider contract."""
   111	        return await self._model.reply(messages)
   112	
   113	    async def next_turn(self, history: Sequence[Turn]) -> PersonaReply:
   114	        """What the persona says next, given everything said so far —
   115	        and whether, having said it, they consider the exchange concluded."""
   116	        return await self.reply_to(self.messages(history))

    51	"""Characters that make a short API key part of a larger ordinary token."""

    63	class ModelFailure(Exception):
    64	    """A model call did not produce words the persona can speak."""

    67	class ModelClient(Protocol):
    68	    """The seam. ``reply`` takes chat-shaped messages — a system prompt
    69	    followed by the conversation so far, persona turns as ``assistant`` and
    70	    the agent's as ``user`` — and returns the persona's next turn.
    71	    ``close`` releases whatever the client holds; always called once the
    72	    simulation is over."""
    73	
    74	    @property
    75	    def model_name(self) -> str: ...
    76	
    77	    async def reply(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply: ...
    78	
    79	    async def close(self) -> None: ...

    82	_SENTENCES = re.compile(r"[^.!?]+[.!?]*")
    83	
    84	
    85	def split_sentences(text: str) -> list[str]:
    86	    """The text, sentence by sentence — the scripted model's whole script."""
    87	    sentences = [sentence.strip() for sentence in _SENTENCES.findall(text)]
    88	    return [sentence for sentence in sentences if sentence] or [text.strip()]

    91	class ScriptedModel:
    92	    """Deterministic persona turns derived from the scenario instructions.
    93	
    94	    Which sentence comes next is read off the messages themselves — the
    95	    count of ``assistant`` turns already spoken — so the reply is a pure
    96	    function of its input and identical across resends, restarts, and
    97	    reruns. When the script is spent, the persona says a fixed goodbye and
    98	    concludes.
    99	    """
   100	
   101	    def __init__(self, scenario_instructions: str) -> None:
   102	        self._script = split_sentences(scenario_instructions)
   103	
   104	    @property
   105	    def model_name(self) -> str:
   106	        return "scripted"
   107	
   108	    async def reply(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply:
   109	        spoken = sum(1 for message in messages if message["role"] == "assistant")
   110	        if spoken < len(self._script):
   111	            return PersonaReply(text=self._script[spoken], concluded=False)
   112	        return PersonaReply(text=GOODBYE, concluded=True)
   113	
   114	    async def close(self) -> None:
   115	        return None

   118	class OpenAICompatibleModel:
   119	    """The direct OpenAI adapter behind the model-client seam.
   120	
   121	    The pinned persona version supplies the model and the claim supplies the
   122	    current key. CI never selects this client.
   123	    """
   124	
   125	    def __init__(
   126	        self,
   127	        *,
   128	        base_url: str,
   129	        api_key: str,
   130	        model_name: str,
   131	        timeout_seconds: float = MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   132	    ) -> None:
   133	        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
   134	        self._api_key = api_key
   135	        self._model_name = model_name
   136	        self._timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout_seconds)
   137	        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None
   138	
   139	    @property
   140	    def model_name(self) -> str:
   141	        return self._model_name
   142	
   143	    def _live_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
   144	        if self._session is None:
   145	            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
   146	        return self._session
   147	
   148	    def _provider_detail(self, value: object) -> str:
   149	        """A bounded provider detail with this client's credential removed.
   150	
   151	        Model failures cross Pipecat's traced service seam. Pipecat records
   152	        exception messages on its native span, before the simulation lifecycle
   153	        applies its process-wide redactor, so the client must remove the key at
   154	        the source.
   155	        """
   156	        rendered = value if isinstance(value, str) else repr(value)
   157	        return self._without_api_key(rendered)[:200]
   158	
   159	    def _without_api_key(self, text: str) -> str:
   160	        """Remove this client's bearer key from provider-authored text.
   161	
   162	        A one-character development key such as ``k`` must not rewrite every
   163	        word containing that letter. Short keys are therefore removed when
   164	        they appear as their own token, which still covers an echoed bearer,
   165	        JSON value, URL parameter, or provider sentence. Real provider keys are
   166	        long enough to replace exactly wherever they occur.
   167	        """
   168	        if not self._api_key:
   169	            return text
   170	        if len(self._api_key) >= 8:
   171	            return text.replace(self._api_key, REDACTED)
   172	        return re.sub(
   173	            rf"(?<![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}]){re.escape(self._api_key)}"
   174	            rf"(?![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}])",
   175	            REDACTED,
   176	            text,
   177	        )
   178	
   179	    async def reply(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply:
   180	        asked = {"model": self._model_name, "messages": messages}
   181	        try:
   182	            async with self._live_session().post(
   183	                f"{self._base_url}/chat/completions",
   184	                json=asked,
   185	                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._api_key}"},
   186	                timeout=self._timeout,
   187	            ) as response:
   188	                if response.status != 200:
   189	                    raise ModelFailure(
   190	                        f"the model answered {response.status}: "
   191	                        f"{self._provider_detail(await response.text())}"
   192	                    )
   193	                body = await response.json()
   194	        except UNREACHABLE as error:
   195	            raise ModelFailure(
   196	                f"the model was unreachable: {self._provider_detail(error)}"
   197	            ) from None
   198	
   199	        try:
   200	            content = body["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
   201	        except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) as unexpected:
   202	            raise ModelFailure(
   203	                "the model's answer had no message content: "
   204	                f"{self._provider_detail(body)}"
   205	            ) from unexpected
   206	        if not isinstance(content, str):
   207	            raise ModelFailure(
   208	                f"the model's content was not text: {self._provider_detail(content)}"
   209	            )
   210	
   211	        content = self._without_api_key(content)
   212	        concluded = CONCLUDE_MARKER in content
   213	        text = content.replace(CONCLUDE_MARKER, "").strip()
   214	        if not text:
   215	            raise ModelFailure("the model's answer had no words to speak")
   216	        return PersonaReply(text=text, concluded=concluded)
   217	
   218	    async def close(self) -> None:
   219	        if self._session is not None:
   220	            await self._session.close()
   221	            self._session = None
   222	
   223	
   224	def build_model_client(
   225	    spec: SimulationSpec,
   226	    *,
   227	    _base_url: str = OPENAI_API_BASE_URL,
   228	) -> ModelClient:
   229	    """Build the pinned persona version's direct LLM adapter.
   230	
   231	    Provider, model, and key come from one required selection. The adapter's
   232	    provider endpoint is fixed here. ``_base_url`` is only the local protocol
   233	    test seam; no deployment input reaches it.
   234	    """
   235	    selected = spec.models.llm
   236	    if selected.provider != "openai" or selected.model != "gpt-4o-mini":
   237	        raise ModelFailure(
   238	            "the claimed persona selected an LLM this simulator does not ship: "
   239	            f"{selected.provider}/{selected.model}"
   240	        )
   241	    if selected.key is None:
   242	        raise ModelFailure("the claimed persona's LLM selection has no direct key")
   243	    return OpenAICompatibleModel(
   244	        base_url=_base_url,
   245	        api_key=selected.key,
   246	        model_name=selected.model,
   247	    )

   247	def _mock_tools(written: list[Any]) -> tuple[MockTool, ...]:

   249	
   250	    The one thing the schema cannot say is that two entries must not name
   251	    the same tool — matching is by name and nothing else, so two answers
   252	    for one name are two answers with no rule to choose between them. It
   253	    is refused rather than resolved here: taking either one silently would
   254	    make the record's answer a matter of which the control plane happened
   255	    to write first.
   256	    """
   257	    named: dict[str, MockTool] = {}
   258	    for entry in written:
   259	        tool_name = entry["tool_name"]
   260	        if tool_name in named:
   261	            raise ContractViolation(
   262	                "spec",
   263	                [

   265	                    "matching is by name alone — there is no rule that would "
   266	                    "choose between them"
   267	                ],
   268	            )
   269	        named[tool_name] = MockTool(
   270	            tool_name=tool_name,
   271	            answer=entry["answer"],
   272	            delay_milliseconds=entry["delay_milliseconds"],
   273	        )
   274	    return tuple(named.values())

1	"""The standing service: claim, conduct, heartbeat, report, repeat.
     2	
     3	One long-poll claim loop asks the control plane for exactly as much work as
     4	the executor has room for. Each claimed spec becomes one running simulation
     5	— a task conducting the exchange, and a task beating every few seconds —
     6	and a cancel directive arriving on a beat's answer stops the conducting at
     7	that beat.
     8	Every arrow points out: the simulator is never dialled into.
     9	
    10	A running simulation writes two records of itself and this is where they
    11	are joined. The lifecycle goes to the control plane as report events; the
    12	conversation goes to the OTLP ingest as spans, authored here from what
    13	whichever conductor ran observed. Neither says what the other says: a
    14	turn, a tool call and a measurement are spans and only spans, and what the
    15	lifecycle carries about them is the one summary fact a reader of a single
    16	simulation asks for — how many turns it reached. Both go through one
    17	reporter, so they are delivered in the order they happened and the
    18	terminal document is last.
    19	
    20	The executor is deliberately a seam. Today it runs each simulation as one
    21	asyncio task in this process; a process- or container-per-simulation
    22	executor implements the same handful of methods and the claim loop never
    23	learns the difference.
    24	
    25	Nothing here may take the whole service down. A control plane that is slow,
    26	broken, or answering nonsense is an ordinary Tuesday, and the loops below
    27	are written so that the worst it costs is the work in flight — never the
    28	simulator itself, and never a capacity slot that no longer comes back.
    29	"""
    30	
    31	from __future__ import annotations
    32	
    33	import asyncio
    34	import contextlib
    35	import logging
    36	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
    37	from typing import Protocol
    38	
    39	from .blob import BlobStore, FilesystemBlobStore, S3BlobStore
    40	from .client import ClaimFailure, ControlPlaneClient, HeartbeatFailure
    41	from .config import MediaSettings, SimulatorConfig
    42	from .contract import ContractViolation
    43	from .model import build_model_client
    44	from .persona import Persona
    45	from .pipeline import Assembled, assemble
    46	from .platform_logging import log_event, simulation_log_context
    47	from .plugs import failed_ending, plug_for
    48	from .redaction import SecretRegistry
    49	from .reporting import Reporter
    50	from .spans import SpanEmitter, trace_id_for
    51	from .spec import SimulationSpec
    52	from .speech import SpeechProviders
    53	from .walk import Conducted, WalkControls, conduct
    54	
    55	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    56	
    57	CLAIM_RETRY_SECONDS = 1.0
    58	
    59	REPEATED_CLAIM_FAILURE_SECONDS = 60.0
    60	"""How often a claim failure that has not changed says so again.
    61	
    62	A control plane that is down fails the same way every retry for as long as
    63	it lasts. Written out each time that is one sentence a second — megabytes
    64	a day of a log nobody can read, with the only thing that would be news, the
    65	failure changing, buried inside it. So a failure speaks up when it is new
    66	and once a minute while it persists; the repeats are still there at DEBUG
    67	for whoever wants to count them."""
    68

    70	def blob_store_for(config: SimulatorConfig) -> BlobStore:
    71	    """Where this simulator's recordings go, decided once at startup.
    72	
    73	    Naming an object-storage endpoint is the whole of what selects it —
    74	    the same shape as naming a media backend, and the reason the entire
    75	    test suite runs against a directory with no container anywhere. The
    76	    two are exclusive because the configuration made them so: a
    77	    deployment with a store has no blob directory to fall back to. One
    78	    place or the other, never both — a copy kept on the container's own
    79	    disk beside the one in the store would hide exactly the fault the
    80	    store is here to fix, until the day a second simulator made half the
    81	    recordings unreadable and nothing said so.
    82	
    83	    Everything above this line is given a :class:`BlobStore` and never
    84	    learns which one it got.
    85	
    86	    The settings are taken apart here rather than handed over whole, so
    87	    that ``blob.py`` stays a leaf: it knows what an object store needs and
    88	    nothing about where a deployment's answers come from. That is what
    89	    lets the seam be tested with five arguments and no environment, and
    90	    what would otherwise make the store's tests configuration's tests too.
    91	    """

    96	        endpoint=store.endpoint,

    99	        secret_access_key=store.secret_access_key,

   104	class Executor(Protocol):
   105	    """The seam between claiming work and running it.
   106	
   107	    ``free_capacity`` is what the next claim declares; ``submit`` accepts a
   108	    spec and returns without waiting for it; ``wait_for_room`` parks the
   109	    claim loop while the executor is full; ``cancel_all`` and ``drain`` are
   110	    teardown. An executor that runs simulations in processes or containers
   111	    implements this same surface and nothing above it changes.
   112	    """
   113	
   114	    @property
   115	    def free_capacity(self) -> int: ...
   116	
   117	    def submit(self, spec: SimulationSpec) -> None: ...
   118	
   119	    async def wait_for_room(self) -> None: ...
   120	
   121	    def cancel_all(self) -> None: ...
   122	
   123	    async def drain(self) -> None: ...

   126	class AsyncioExecutor:
   127	    """Runs each simulation as one asyncio task inside this process.
   128	
   129	    The first executor, and the simplest thing that honors the seam: a
   130	    testing platform's failure domain is forgiving, and per-simulation
   131	    containers would tax exactly the self-hosted deployment where adoption
   132	    lives. Heavier executors can replace this without touching the loop.
   133	    """
   134	
   135	    def __init__(
   136	        self, capacity: int, *, start: Callable[[SimulationSpec], Awaitable[None]]
   137	    ) -> None:
   138	        self._capacity = capacity
   139	        self._start = start
   140	        self._running: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
   141	        self._room = asyncio.Event()
   142	        self._room.set()
   143	
   144	    @property
   145	    def free_capacity(self) -> int:
   146	        return self._capacity - len(self._running)

   148	    def submit(self, spec: SimulationSpec) -> None:
   149	        if self.free_capacity < 1:
   150	            raise RuntimeError("submit called with no free capacity")
   151	        task = asyncio.create_task(
   152	            self._start(spec), name=f"simulation:{spec.simulation_id}"
   153	        )
   154	        self._running.add(task)
   155	        task.add_done_callback(self._finished)
   156	        if self.free_capacity < 1:
   157	            self._room.clear()
   158	
   159	    def _finished(self, task: asyncio.Task) -> None:
   160	        self._running.discard(task)
   161	        self._room.set()
   162	        if not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is not None:
   163	            simulation_id = task.get_name().removeprefix("simulation:")
   164	            fault = task.exception()
   165	            assert fault is not None
   166	            log_event(
   167	                logger,
   168	                logging.ERROR,
   169	                "egma.simulation.finished",
   170	                "simulation task died before it could report",
   171	                attributes={
   172	                    "egma.simulation_id": simulation_id,
   173	                    "egma.outcome": "failed",
   174	                    "error.type": type(fault).__name__,
   175	                },
   176	                exc_info=fault,
   177	            )
   178	
   179	    async def wait_for_room(self) -> None:
   180	        await self._room.wait()
   181	
   182	    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
   183	        for task in list(self._running):
   184	            task.cancel()
   185	
   186	    async def drain(self) -> None:
   187	        while self._running:
   188	            await asyncio.gather(*list(self._running), return_exceptions=True)

   191	class RunningSimulation:
   192	    """One claimed spec being conducted, and its heartbeat.
   193	
   194	    It is also the one place that sees everything a conductor observes,
   195	    which is why the conversation's spans are authored here rather than
   196	    deeper in. There are two conductors and they observe in two
   197	    currencies: the walk sees a turn at the moment it happened, and the
   198	    voice conductor sees both ends of one, read off the audio. Both report
   199	    to the callbacks below, and what comes out is one emitter for chat and
   200	    voice alike.

   202

   219	            client,

   227	        # alongside it.

   104	class Executor(Protocol):
   105	    """The seam between claiming work and running it.

   107	    ``free_capacity`` is what the next claim declares; ``submit`` accepts a
   108	    spec and returns without waiting for it; ``wait_for_room`` parks the

   126	class AsyncioExecutor:
   127	    """Runs each simulation as one asyncio task inside this process.
   128

   130	    testing platform's failure domain is forgiving, and per-simulation

1	"""Reporting: everything minted as it happens, delivered in order, at least once.
     2	
     3	One ``Reporter`` serves one simulation and carries two kinds of document
     4	to the control plane: the lifecycle report events, and the conversation
     5	itself as OTLP span batches. Both are stamped and serialized at the moment
     6	they happen; the serialized bytes are appended to a local write-ahead log
     7	and then posted by a single sender task, so delivery is ordered and a
     8	resend replays byte-identical documents — ids and timestamps included,
     9	which lets the control plane dedup report event ids and ClickHouse suppress a
    10	recent exact repeat of an insert block. The report schema is applied to every report
    11	document before it is logged or sent: an invalid report is a bug in this
    12	process, and it fails here, loudly, rather than at the receiver.
    13	
    14	**One queue for both kinds, and that is the design rather than a saving.**
    15	Because span batches and lifecycle documents share the one ordered sender,
    16	the terminal report leaves only after every span batch minted before it
    17	landed. So when the control plane records a simulation terminal, the
    18	evidence a grader will read is already in the trace store — there is no
    19	window in which a conversation is finished and its transcript is still in
    20	flight.
    21	
    22	The log on disk holds both, interleaved in the order the events happened,
    23	each line exactly the bytes that went on the wire. The two kinds are told
    24	apart by their own shape — a report names its ``contract_version``, a span
    25	batch its ``resourceSpans`` — because a log line that was not what was
    26	sent would not be a record of what was sent.
    27	
    28	A document that will not go through is resent, same bytes, with widening
    29	backoff until a deadline. Past that the reporter is *abandoned*: it stops
    30	trying, and the log on disk is the only record of what this simulation
    31	saw. That is bounded rather than endless on purpose — retrying forever
    32	would hold a capacity slot open through an outage of any length, and a
    33	simulator the control plane cannot hear is exactly what its heartbeat
    34	sweep exists to notice.
    35	"""
    36	
    37	from __future__ import annotations
    38	
    39	import asyncio
    40	import hashlib
    41	import json
    42	import logging
    43	import re

    55	# restarting, then stops. Bounded on purpose: retrying forever would hold a
    56	# simulation's capacity slot open through an outage of any length, and the
    57	# control plane already has an honest answer for a simulator gone quiet —
    58	# the heartbeat sweep. The write-ahead log keeps the bytes either way.

     1	"""Reporting: everything minted as it happens, delivered in order, at least once.
     2	
     3	One ``Reporter`` serves one simulation and carries two kinds of document
     4	to the control plane: the lifecycle report events, and the conversation
     5	itself as OTLP span batches. Both are stamped and serialized at the moment
     6	they happen; the serialized bytes are appended to a local write-ahead log
     7	and then posted by a single sender task, so delivery is ordered and a
     8	resend replays byte-identical documents — ids and timestamps included,
     9	which lets the control plane dedup report event ids and ClickHouse suppress a
    10	recent exact repeat of an insert block. The report schema is applied to every report
    11	document before it is logged or sent: an invalid report is a bug in this
    12	process, and it fails here, loudly, rather than at the receiver.
    13	
    14	**One queue for both kinds, and that is the design rather than a saving.**
    15	Because span batches and lifecycle documents share the one ordered sender,
    16	the terminal report leaves only after every span batch minted before it
    17	landed. So when the control plane records a simulation terminal, the
    18	evidence a grader will read is already in the trace store — there is no
    19	window in which a conversation is finished and its transcript is still in
    20	flight.
    21	
    22	The log on disk holds both, interleaved in the order the events happened,
    23	each line exactly the bytes that went on the wire. The two kinds are told
    24	apart by their own shape — a report names its ``contract_version``, a span
    25	batch its ``resourceSpans`` — because a log line that was not what was
    26	sent would not be a record of what was sent.
    27	
    28	A document that will not go through is resent, same bytes, with widening
    29	backoff until a deadline. Past that the reporter is *abandoned*: it stops
    30	trying, and the log on disk is the only record of what this simulation
    31	saw. That is bounded rather than endless on purpose — retrying forever
    32	would hold a capacity slot open through an outage of any length, and a
    33	simulator the control plane cannot hear is exactly what its heartbeat
    34	sweep exists to notice.
    35	"""

1	"""A claimed spec, as a thing with parts rather than a bag of keys.
     2	
     3	A spec arrives as JSON and is held to the contract's schema before anything
     4	is done with it. Past that gate it becomes this: a small frozen record whose
     5	fields say what they hold, so the code that conducts a simulation asks for
     6	``spec.limits.max_turns`` instead of walking three dictionaries deep and
     7	trusting that each step is there.
     8	
     9	The gate and the type are deliberately the same step. Nothing builds one of
    10	these without validating first, which is what lets every reader below take
    11	the fields at face value.
    12	"""
    13	
    14	from __future__ import annotations
    15	
    16	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    17	from typing import Any
    18	
    19	from .contract import ContractViolation, validate_spec
    20	
    21	
    22	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    23	class MockTool:
    24	    """One tool name, and what egma answers when the agent calls it.
    25	
    26	    Already resolved when it arrives: the control plane worked the
    27	    project's defaults and the test's overrides into one answer per name
    28	    at run creation, so every simulation in one run sees one world and
    29	    there is nothing left here to merge.
    30	    """
    31	
    32	    tool_name: str
    33	    """The agent's own name for the tool, verbatim — the whole of how a
    34	    call is matched, and never parsed or folded."""
    35	
    36	    answer: dict[str, Any]
    37	    """What is served, in the shape it was authored in: ``{"answer": …}``
    38	    with the value the tool returns, or ``{"error": …}`` with the failure
    39	    it raises. Held whole rather than unpacked, so the bytes that go on
    40	    the wire are the bytes that were authored."""
    41	
    42	    delay_milliseconds: int
    43	    """How long egma holds the answer back, so a mocked backend takes as
    44	    long as the real one would."""
    45	
    46	    @property
    47	    def fails(self) -> bool:
    48	        """Whether this answer is the failure branch."""
    49	        return "error" in self.answer
    50	
    51	
    52	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    53	class PlatformCarrier:
    54	    """The SIP trunk a deployment uses for phone simulations.
    55	
    56	    The media backend is deployment configuration. It cannot ride this
    57	    block and cannot be selected by a work order.
    58	    """
    59	
    60	    trunk_address: str | None = None
    61	    trunk_number: str | None = None
    62	    trunk_username: str | None = None
    63	    trunk_password: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    64	
    65	
    66	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    67	class PlatformSettings:
    68	    """The carrier part of deployment configuration on this work order."""
    69	
    70	    carrier: PlatformCarrier = field(default_factory=PlatformCarrier)
    71	
    72	    @property
    73	    def secrets(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    74	        """Every secret these settings hold, for redaction.
    75	
    76	        One place to ask, exactly as the configuration's own secrets have
    77	        one, so a fourth key arriving cannot fall out of the scrubbing.
    78	        """
    79	        password = self.carrier.trunk_password
    80	        return () if password is None else (password,)
    81	
    82	    @classmethod
    83	    def from_document(cls, written: Any) -> PlatformSettings:
    84	        """The platform block of a validated spec, or the empty settings.
    85	
    86	        The schema has already refused a field nobody writes, so the reads
    87	        below take what is there at face value — the same bargain the rest
    88	        of this module makes.
    89	        """
    90	        block = written or {}
    91	        carrier = block.get("carrier") or {}
    92	        return cls(
    93	            carrier=PlatformCarrier(
    94	                trunk_address=carrier.get("trunk_address"),
    95	                trunk_number=carrier.get("trunk_number"),
    96	                trunk_username=carrier.get("trunk_username"),
    97	                trunk_password=carrier.get("trunk_password"),
    98	            ),
    99	        )
   100	
   101	
   102	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   103	class ModelSelection:
   104	    """One pinned provider/model pair and its direct credential, when used."""
   105	
   106	    provider: str
   107	    model: str
   108	    key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
   109

   111	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   112	class SpeechSelection(ModelSelection):
   113	    """The TTS selection and the technical voice it owns."""
   114	
   115	    voice_id: str = ""
   116	    speed: float = 1.0
   117	
   118	
   119	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   120	class SelectedModels:
   121	    """The complete model selection from the pinned persona version."""
   122	
   123	    llm: ModelSelection
   124	    stt: ModelSelection
   125	    tts: SpeechSelection
   126	
   127	    @property
   128	    def secrets(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   129	        """Every direct provider credential carried by this work order."""
   130	        return tuple(key for key in (self.llm.key, self.stt.key, self.tts.key) if key)

   132	    @classmethod

   134	        """Read the required, already validated model block."""
   135	        tts = written["tts"]
   136	        return cls(
   137	            llm=_selection(written["llm"]),
   138	            stt=_selection(written["stt"]),
   139	            tts=SpeechSelection(
   140	                provider=tts["provider"],
   141	                model=tts["model"],
   142	                key=tts.get("key"),
   143	                voice_id=tts["voice_id"],
   144	                speed=float(tts["speed"]),
   145	            ),
   146	        )

   151	        provider=written["provider"],
   152	        model=written["model"],
   153	        key=written.get("key"),
   154	    )
   155	
   156	
   157	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   158	class Limits:
   159	    """The walls around one simulation, from the spec that claimed it.
   160	
   161	    A limit tripping ends the simulation deliberately — reported as
   162	    ``limit_reached``, which is never the agent failing.
   163	    """
   164	
   165	    max_duration_seconds: int
   166	    max_turns: int
   167	
   168	
   169	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   170	class SimulationSpec:
   171	    """One claimable simulation, fully flattened — nothing left to resolve."""
   172	
   173	    simulation_id: str
   174	    """Opaque to the simulator: never parsed, never minted, never rewritten."""
   175	
   176	    modality: str
   177	    """``chat`` or ``voice``. Selects the pipeline legs, not the persona."""
   178	
   179	    scenario_instructions: str
   180	    """What the persona wants on this occasion, from the test's own content."""
   181	
   182	    limits: Limits
   183	
   184	    persona_traits: dict[str, Any]
   185	    """The persona version's complete authored human traits."""
   186	
   187	    agent_platform: str | None
   188	    """What runs the agent. Provenance only; never adapter dispatch."""
   189	
   190	    connection_type: str
   191	    """Which adapter reaches the agent. An open vocabulary, not an enum."""
   192	
   193	    access_variant: str
   194	    """Which explicit authority and config path the adapter uses."""
   195	
   196	    connection_config: dict[str, Any]
   197	    """The non-secret reach configuration; its keys belong to the plug."""
   198	
   199	    credentials: Any
   200	    """Secret material, or None. Held in memory, handed only to the plug."""
   201	
   202	    models: SelectedModels
   203	    """The only source for LLM, STT, TTS, and technical voice choices."""
   204	
   205	    mock_tools: tuple[MockTool, ...] = ()
   206	    """What egma answers for while this simulation runs, already resolved.
   207	
   208	    Empty is the ordinary case and means egma answers for nothing: every
   209	    tool the agent has runs its own implementation, untouched and
   210	    unobserved.
   211	    """
   212	
   213	    platform: PlatformSettings = field(default_factory=PlatformSettings)
   214	    """The optional SIP carrier block. It owns no model or voice choice."""
   215	
   216	    @classmethod
   217	    def from_document(cls, document: Any) -> SimulationSpec:
   218	        """Hold a claimed document to the contract, then read it.
   219	
   220	        Raises ``ContractViolation`` if the document does not speak the
   221	        contract — which is a refusal to conduct, not a simulation that
   222	        went wrong.
   223	        """
   224	        validate_spec(document)
   225	        connection = document["connection"]
   226	        limits = document["limits"]
   227	        return cls(
   228	            mock_tools=_mock_tools(document.get("mock_tools") or []),
   229	            platform=PlatformSettings.from_document(document.get("platform")),
   230	            models=SelectedModels.from_document(document["models"]),
   231	            simulation_id=document["simulation_id"],
   232	            modality=document["modality"],
   233	            scenario_instructions=document["scenario"]["instructions"],
   234	            limits=Limits(
   235	                max_duration_seconds=limits["max_duration_seconds"],
   236	                max_turns=limits["max_turns"],
   237	            ),
   238	            persona_traits=document["persona"]["traits"],
   239	            agent_platform=connection["agent_platform"],
   240	            connection_type=connection["connection_type"],
   241	            access_variant=connection["access_variant"],
   242	            connection_config=connection["config"],
   243	            credentials=connection["credentials"],
   244	        )
   245	
   246	
   247	def _mock_tools(written: list[Any]) -> tuple[MockTool, ...]:
   248	    """The resolved answers, one per tool name.
   249	
   250	    The one thing the schema cannot say is that two entries must not name
   251	    the same tool — matching is by name and nothing else, so two answers
   252	    for one name are two answers with no rule to choose between them. It
   253	    is refused rather than resolved here: taking either one silently would
   254	    make the record's answer a matter of which the control plane happened
   255	    to write first.
   256	    """
   257	    named: dict[str, MockTool] = {}
   258	    for entry in written:
   259	        tool_name = entry["tool_name"]
   260	        if tool_name in named:
   261	            raise ContractViolation(
   262	                "spec",
   263	                [
   264	                    f"/mock_tools: {tool_name!r} is answered twice, and "
   265	                    "matching is by name alone — there is no rule that would "
   266	                    "choose between them"
   267	                ],
   268	            )
   269	        named[tool_name] = MockTool(
   270	            tool_name=tool_name,
   271	            answer=entry["answer"],
   272	            delay_milliseconds=entry["delay_milliseconds"],
   273	        )
   274	    return tuple(named.values())

1	"""One simulation walks one exchange: persona and plug, turn by turn.
     2	
     3	The walk is the plug-blind, model-blind middle: it opens the exchange
     4	through the plug, lets the persona and the agent alternate, records every
     5	turn as it flows, measures each answer, and names how it all ended. Four
     6	deliberate endings — the persona concluding, the agent ending, the turn
     7	limit, the duration limit — plus the cancel directive; each is reported
     8	distinctly, and a limit ending is never the agent failing.
     9	
    10	Two hands may stop a running walk from outside its own loop: a cancel
    11	directive honored at a heartbeat, and the duration watchdog. Both act
    12	through :class:`WalkControls`, and the first cause to land is the one the
    13	record shows — a cause arriving after the walk already ended changes
    14	nothing, because what happened is the record.
    15	"""
    16	
    17	from __future__ import annotations
    18	
    19	import asyncio
    20	import contextlib
    21	import logging
    22	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Coroutine
    23	from dataclasses import dataclass
    24	from typing import Any
    25	
    26	from .persona import Persona, Turn
    27	from .plugs import ConnectionPlug
    28	
    29	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    30	
    31	OnTurn = Callable[[str, str], Awaitable[None]]
    32	OnTiming = Callable[[str, float], Awaitable[None]]
    33	OnToolCall = Callable[[str, str | None], Awaitable[None]]
    34	
    35	OnAnswered = Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]
    36	"""Everything one agent answer produced is on the record — the words it
    37	carried, the tool calls it made, the time it took.
    38	
    39	It carries nothing, because it is not an observation: it is the boundary
    40	between one answer and the next, and turn-taking is the only thing that
    41	knows where that falls. An answer that produced no words is still an
    42	answer that ended, which is exactly the case a reader of the turns alone
    43	would miss. An agent that speaks first has finished saying its piece the
    44	same way, so the opening counts as one.
    45	
    46	The last answer of a conversation is deliberately not announced: the walk
    47	is over, and whatever it produced belongs with the record of the whole
    48	thing rather than in a boundary of its own."""
    49	
    50	# The two causes a WalkControls can carry. Writer and reader both name
    51	# these constants, so a stop can never be misread as the other cause.
    52	CANCEL_DIRECTIVE = "cancel directive"
    53	DURATION_LIMIT = "duration limit"
    54	
    55	
    56	class _WalkStopped(Exception):
    57	    """Internal: a stop cause landed while the walk awaited something."""
    58	
    59	
    60	class WalkControls:
    61	    """The two hands that may stop a walk, and the record of which did."""
    62	
    63	    def __init__(self) -> None:
    64	        self._stopped = asyncio.Event()
    65	        self.cause: str | None = None
    66	
    67	    def request_cancel(self) -> None:
    68	        """A cancel directive, honored at the walk's next opportunity."""
    69	        self._stop_for(CANCEL_DIRECTIVE)
    70	
    71	    def trip_duration_limit(self) -> None:
    72	        self._stop_for(DURATION_LIMIT)
    73	
    74	    def _stop_for(self, cause: str) -> None:
    75	        if self.cause is None:
    76	            self.cause = cause
    77	            self._stopped.set()
    78	
    79	    async def guard(self, coroutine: Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]) -> Any:
    80	        """Await one step of the walk, unless a stop cause lands first.
    81	
    82	        The step runs as its own task, raced against the stop signal; when
    83	        the stop wins, the step is cancelled and ``_WalkStopped`` raised so
    84	        the walk can name the cause. Cancellation of the walk itself — the
    85	        service tearing down — passes straight through.
    86	        """
    87	        step = asyncio.ensure_future(coroutine)
    88	        interrupter = asyncio.ensure_future(self._stopped.wait())
    89	        try:
    90	            done, _pending = await asyncio.wait(
    91	                {step, interrupter}, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
    92	            )
    93	        except asyncio.CancelledError:
    94	            step.cancel()
    95	            raise
    96	        finally:
    97	            interrupter.cancel()
    98	            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
    99	                await interrupter
   100

   145	AGENT_ENDED: Ending = ("agent_ended", "the agent ended the exchange")
   146	
   147	
   148	def turn_limit_reached(max_turns: int) -> Ending:
   149	    """The turn limit tripped, named with the budget that ran out."""
   150	    return "limit_reached", f"the turn limit ({max_turns} turns) tripped"
   151	
   152	
   153	def duration_limit_reached(max_duration_seconds: float) -> Ending:
   154	    """The duration limit tripped, named with the budget that ran out."""
   155	    return (
   156	        "limit_reached",
   157	        f"the duration limit ({max_duration_seconds}s) tripped",
   158	    )
   159	
   160	
   161	async def conduct(
   162	    *,
   163	    persona: Persona,
   164	    plug: ConnectionPlug,
   165	    max_turns: int,
   166	    max_duration_seconds: float,
   167	    on_turn: OnTurn,
   168	    on_timing: OnTiming | None,
   169	    controls: WalkControls,
   170	    name: str,
   171	    on_tool_call: OnToolCall | None = None,
   172	    on_answered: OnAnswered | None = None,
   173	) -> Conducted:
   174	    """Walk one simulation through one exchange, and say how it went."""
   175	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
   176	    history: list[Turn] = []
   177	
   178	    async def record(speaker: str, text: str) -> None:
   179	        history.append(Turn(speaker, text))
   180	        await on_turn(speaker, text)
   181	
   182	    async def answered() -> None:
   183	        if on_answered is not None:
   184	            await on_answered()
   185	
   186	    def budget_spent() -> bool:
   187	        return len(history) >= max_turns
   188	
   189	    def ended(named: Ending) -> Conducted:
   190	        ending, reason = named
   191	        return Conducted(
   192	            status="completed",
   193	            ending=ending,
   194	            reason=reason,
   195	            provider_reference=plug.provider_reference,
   196	        )
   197	
   198	    def limit_by_turns() -> Conducted:
   199	        return ended(turn_limit_reached(max_turns))
   200	
   201	    watchdog = asyncio.create_task(
   202	        _duration_watchdog(max_duration_seconds, controls),
   203	        name=f"{name}:watchdog",
   204	    )
   205	    try:
   206	        greeting = await controls.guard(plug.open())
   207	        if greeting is not None:
   208	            await record("agent", greeting)
   209	        await answered()
   210	
   211	        while True:
   212	            # The persona's move — unless the budget is already spent.
   213	            if budget_spent():
   214	                return limit_by_turns()
   215	            reply = await controls.guard(persona.next_turn(history))
   216	            await record("human", reply.text)
   217	            if reply.concluded:
   218	                return ended(PERSONA_CONCLUDED)
   219	
   220	            # The agent's move — not asked for when its answer could not
   221	            # be recorded anyway: the limit ends the walk before a phantom
   222	            # exchange happens off the record.
   223	            if budget_spent():
   224	                return limit_by_turns()
   225	            asked_at = loop.time()
   226	            answer = await controls.guard(plug.deliver(reply.text))
   227	            if on_timing is not None:
   228	                await on_timing(
   229	                    "turn_response_latency", (loop.time() - asked_at) * 1000
   230	                )
   231	            # What the agent did while answering, before what it said: a
   232	            # tool call happened during the turn, and only a platform that
   233	            # exposes one reports any at all.
   234	            if on_tool_call is not None:
   235	                for call in answer.tool_calls:
   236	                    await on_tool_call(call.name, call.arguments)
   237	            if answer.text is not None:
   238	                await record("agent", answer.text)
   239	            if answer.ended:
   240	                return ended(AGENT_ENDED)
   241	            # The answer is whole, whatever it turned out to carry. Said
   242	            # here rather than beside the turn above, because an answer
   243	            # with no words is still an answer, and a boundary read off
   244	            # the transcript alone would miss exactly that one.
   245	            await answered()
   246	    except _WalkStopped:
   247	        if controls.cause == CANCEL_DIRECTIVE:
   248	            return Conducted(
   249	                status="canceled",
   250	                ending="canceled",
   251	                reason=None,
   252	                provider_reference=plug.provider_reference,
   253	            )
   254	        return ended(duration_limit_reached(max_duration_seconds))
   255	    finally:
   256	        watchdog.cancel()
   257	        with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
   258	            await watchdog
   259	        await _close_quietly(plug, name)
   260	
   261	
   262	async def _duration_watchdog(
   263	    max_duration_seconds: float, controls: WalkControls
   264	) -> None:
   265	    await asyncio.sleep(max_duration_seconds)
   266	    controls.trip_duration_limit()
   267	
   268	
   269	async def _close_quietly(plug: ConnectionPlug, name: str) -> None:
   270	    """Tear the exchange down; a failure to close is logged, never raised —
   271	    it would otherwise eat the walk's own answer."""
   272	    try:
   273	        await plug.close()
   274	    except asyncio.CancelledError:
   275	        raise
   276	    except Exception:
   277	        logger.exception("closing the exchange for %s failed", name)

   267	        # each recorder update and its position map indivisible.

   323	        """Close input after the recorder has written every earlier frame."""

   325	            if (
   326	                self._closing_source_end is not None

   328	            ):

   334	    def _maybe_close_input(self) -> None:
   335	        if (
   336	            self._closing_source_end is not None
   337	            and self._processed_source_end >= self._closing_source_end
   338	        ):
   339	            self._input_closed = True

   341	    @property

   346	        # pinned in uv.lock and covered by the frame-level alignment test.
   347	        return Fraction(len(self._bot_audio_buffer) // 2, self.sample_rate)
   348	
   349	    @property
   350	    def position(self) -> MediaPosition:
   351	        if not self.sample_rate:
   352	            return Fraction(0)
   353	        samples = max(len(self._user_audio_buffer), len(self._bot_audio_buffer)) // 2
   354	        return Fraction(samples, self.sample_rate)
   355	
   356	    async def agent_interval(
   357	        self,
   358	        source_began: MediaPosition,
   359	        source_ended: MediaPosition,
   360	        *,
   361	        observed_through: MediaPosition,
   362	    ) -> tuple[MediaPosition, MediaPosition]:
   363	        """Place one agent turn on Pipecat's canonical recorded track."""
   364	        async with self._recording_ready:
   365	            while True:
   366	                if self._processed_source_end < observed_through:
   367	                    await self._recording_ready.wait()
   368	                    continue
   369	                began = self._agent_position(source_began, at_turn_start=True)
   370	                ended = self._agent_position(source_ended, at_turn_start=False)
   371	                if began is not None and ended is not None:
   372	                    return began, ended
   373	                if began is None and self._mapped_past(
   374	                    source_began, at_turn_start=True
   375	                ):
   376	                    raise SpeechFault(
   377	                        "agent turn began in audio Pipecat did not record"
   378	                    )
   379	                if ended is None and self._mapped_past(
   380	                    source_ended, at_turn_start=False
   381	                ):
   382	                    raise SpeechFault(
   383	                        "agent turn ended in audio Pipecat did not record"
   384	                    )
   385	                if self._input_closed:
   386	                    if began is None:
   387	                        raise SpeechFault(
   388	                            "agent turn began after Pipecat's recording ended"
   389	                        )
   390	                    return began, self._final_agent_end(source_ended)
   391	                await self._recording_ready.wait()
   392	
   393	    def _agent_position(
   394	        self, source_position: MediaPosition, *, at_turn_start: bool
   395	    ) -> MediaPosition | None:
   396	        """At a gap, starts use later audio and ends use earlier audio."""
   397	        if not self.sample_rate:
   398	            return None
   399	        segments = (
   400	            reversed(self._input_segments)
   401	            if at_turn_start
   402	            else self._input_segments
   403	        )
   404	        for segment in segments:
   405	            inside = (
   406	                segment.source_start <= source_position < segment.source_end
   407	                if at_turn_start
   408	                else segment.source_start < source_position <= segment.source_end
   409	            )
   410	            if inside:
   411	                return Fraction(
   412	                    segment.recording_start_sample, self.sample_rate
   413	                ) + (source_position - segment.source_start)
   414	        return None
   415	
   416	    def _mapped_past(
   417	        self, source_position: MediaPosition, *, at_turn_start: bool
   418	    ) -> bool:
   419	        if not self._input_segments:
   420	            return False
