   213	class _EvidenceRecorder(AudioBufferProcessor):
   214	    """Expose Pipecat's canonical recording cursor to the transcript."""
   215	
   216	    def __init__(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
   217	        super().__init__(**kwargs)
   218	        self._recording_ready = asyncio.Condition()
   219	        self._resampled_input: dict[int, tuple[int, float]] = {}
   220	        self._processed_source_end = Fraction(0)
   221	        self._last_input_frame_duration = Fraction(0)
   222	        self._input_segments: list[_RecordedInputSegment] = []
   223	        self._closing_source_end: MediaPosition | None = None
   224	        self._input_closed = False
   225	
   226	    async def _resample_input_audio(self, frame: InputAudioRawFrame) -> bytes:
   227	        audio = await super()._resample_input_audio(frame)
   228	        self._resampled_input[frame.id] = (
   229	            len(audio) // 2,
   230	            self._input_resampler_delay(),
   231	        )
   232	        return audio
   233	
   234	    def _input_resampler_delay(self) -> float:
   235	        """Read the exact pending output from Pipecat's pinned recorder."""
   236	        resampler = getattr(self, "_input_resampler", None)
   237	        if not isinstance(resampler, SOXRStreamAudioResampler):
   238	            raise SpeechFault(
   239	                "the pinned pipecat release changed its recording resampler"
   240	            )
   241	        stream = getattr(resampler, "_soxr_stream", None)
   242	        if stream is None:
   243	            return 0.0
   244	        delay = float(stream.delay())
   245	        if delay < 0 or not math.isfinite(delay):
   246	            raise SpeechFault(
   247	                "the pinned pipecat release returned an invalid resampler delay"
   248	            )
   249	        return delay
   250	
   251	    @staticmethod
   252	    def _source_range(
   253	        frame: InputAudioRawFrame,
   254	    ) -> tuple[MediaPosition, MediaPosition]:
   255	        source_range = frame.metadata.get(_INPUT_SOURCE_RANGE)
   256	        if (
   257	            not isinstance(source_range, tuple)
   258	            or len(source_range) != 2
   259	            or not all(isinstance(value, Fraction) for value in source_range)
   260	        ):
   261	            raise SpeechFault("agent audio reached the recorder without its position")
   262	        return cast(tuple[MediaPosition, MediaPosition], source_range)
   263	
   264	    async def _process_recording(self, frame: Frame) -> None:
   265	        # Input audio is a Pipecat SystemFrame while output audio is a normal
   266	        # frame, so Pipecat can present both to this processor at once. Keep
   267	        # each recorder update and its position map indivisible.
   268	        async with self._recording_ready:
   269	            if isinstance(frame, InputAudioRawFrame) and self._input_closed:
   270	                raise SpeechFault("agent audio arrived after its recorded input ended")
   271	            await super()._process_recording(frame)
   272	            if not isinstance(frame, InputAudioRawFrame):
   273	                return
   274	            source_start, source_end = self._source_range(frame)
   275	            if source_start != self._processed_source_end or source_end < source_start:
   276	                raise SpeechFault("agent audio reached the recorder out of order")
   277	            try:
   278	                written, pending = self._resampled_input.pop(frame.id)
   279	            except KeyError as changed:
   280	                raise SpeechFault(
   281	                    "the pinned pipecat release skipped its recording resampler"
   282	                ) from changed
   283	            if written:
   284	                represented_end_samples = (
   285	                    float(source_end * self.sample_rate) - pending
   286	                )
   287	                rounded_end = round(represented_end_samples)
   288	                if abs(represented_end_samples - rounded_end) > 1e-6:
   289	                    raise SpeechFault(
   290	                        "pipecat's recording resampler returned an invalid position"
   291	                    )
   292	                represented_end = Fraction(rounded_end, self.sample_rate)
   293	                represented_start = represented_end - Fraction(
   294	                    written, self.sample_rate
   295	                )
   296	                recording_end = len(self._user_audio_buffer) // 2
   297	                recording_start = recording_end - written
   298	                if represented_start < 0 or represented_end > source_end:
   299	                    raise SpeechFault(
   300	                        "pipecat's recording resampler returned an invalid position"
   301	                    )
   302	                if (
   303	                    self._input_segments
   304	                    and represented_start < self._input_segments[-1].source_end
   305	                ):
   306	                    raise SpeechFault(
   307	                        "pipecat's recording resampler moved agent audio backwards"
   308	                    )
   309	                self._input_segments.append(
   310	                    _RecordedInputSegment(
   311	                        source_start=represented_start,
   312	                        source_end=represented_end,
   313	                        recording_start_sample=recording_start,
   314	                        recording_end_sample=recording_end,
   315	                    )
   316	                )
   317	            self._processed_source_end = source_end
   318	            self._last_input_frame_duration = source_end - source_start
   319	            self._maybe_close_input()
   320	            self._recording_ready.notify_all()
   321	
   322	    async def close_input_at(self, source_end: MediaPosition) -> None:
   323	        """Close input after the recorder has written every earlier frame."""
   324	        async with self._recording_ready:
   325	            if (
   326	                self._closing_source_end is not None
   327	                and self._closing_source_end != source_end
   328	            ):
   329	                raise SpeechFault("agent input ended at two different positions")
   330	            self._closing_source_end = source_end
   331	            self._maybe_close_input()
   332	            self._recording_ready.notify_all()
   333	
   334	    def _maybe_close_input(self) -> None:
   335	        if (
   336	            self._closing_source_end is not None
   337	            and self._processed_source_end >= self._closing_source_end
   338	        ):
   339	            self._input_closed = True
   340	
   341	    @property
   342	    def bot_position(self) -> MediaPosition:
   343	        if not self.sample_rate:
   344	            return Fraction(0)
   345	        # Pipecat 1.7.0 has no public current-output cursor. This one access is
   346	        # pinned in uv.lock and covered by the frame-level alignment test.
   347	        return Fraction(len(self._bot_audio_buffer) // 2, self.sample_rate)
   348	
   349	    @property
   350	    def position(self) -> MediaPosition:
   351	        if not self.sample_rate:
   352	            return Fraction(0)
   353	        samples = max(len(self._user_audio_buffer), len(self._bot_audio_buffer)) // 2
   354	        return Fraction(samples, self.sample_rate)
   355	
   356	    async def agent_interval(
   357	        self,
   358	        source_began: MediaPosition,
   359	        source_ended: MediaPosition,
   360	        *,
   361	        observed_through: MediaPosition,
   362	    ) -> tuple[MediaPosition, MediaPosition]:
   363	        """Place one agent turn on Pipecat's canonical recorded track."""
   364	        async with self._recording_ready:
   365	            while True:
   366	                if self._processed_source_end < observed_through:
   367	                    await self._recording_ready.wait()
   368	                    continue
   369	                began = self._agent_position(source_began, at_turn_start=True)
   370	                ended = self._agent_position(source_ended, at_turn_start=False)
   371	                if began is not None and ended is not None:
   372	                    return began, ended
   373	                if began is None and self._mapped_past(
   374	                    source_began, at_turn_start=True
   375	                ):
   376	                    raise SpeechFault(
   377	                        "agent turn began in audio Pipecat did not record"
   378	                    )
   379	                if ended is None and self._mapped_past(
   380	                    source_ended, at_turn_start=False
   381	                ):
   382	                    raise SpeechFault(
   383	                        "agent turn ended in audio Pipecat did not record"
   384	                    )
   385	                if self._input_closed:
   386	                    if began is None:
   387	                        raise SpeechFault(
   388	                            "agent turn began after Pipecat's recording ended"
   389	                        )
   390	                    return began, self._final_agent_end(source_ended)
   391	                await self._recording_ready.wait()
   392	
   393	    def _agent_position(
   394	        self, source_position: MediaPosition, *, at_turn_start: bool
   395	    ) -> MediaPosition | None:
   396	        """At a gap, starts use later audio and ends use earlier audio."""
   397	        if not self.sample_rate:
   398	            return None
   399	        segments = (
   400	            reversed(self._input_segments)
   401	            if at_turn_start
   402	            else self._input_segments
   403	        )
   404	        for segment in segments:
   405	            inside = (
   406	                segment.source_start <= source_position < segment.source_end
   407	                if at_turn_start
   408	                else segment.source_start < source_position <= segment.source_end
   409	            )
   410	            if inside:
   411	                return Fraction(
   412	                    segment.recording_start_sample, self.sample_rate
   413	                ) + (source_position - segment.source_start)
   414	        return None
   415	
   416	    def _mapped_past(
   417	        self, source_position: MediaPosition, *, at_turn_start: bool
   418	    ) -> bool:
   419	        if not self._input_segments:
   420	            return False

1	"""The standing service: claim, conduct, heartbeat, report, repeat.
     2	
     3	One long-poll claim loop asks the control plane for exactly as much work as
     4	the executor has room for. Each claimed spec becomes one running simulation
     5	— a task conducting the exchange, and a task beating every few seconds —
     6	and a cancel directive arriving on a beat's answer stops the conducting at
     7	that beat.
     8	Every arrow points out: the simulator is never dialled into.
     9	
    10	A running simulation writes two records of itself and this is where they
    11	are joined. The lifecycle goes to the control plane as report events; the
    12	conversation goes to the OTLP ingest as spans, authored here from what
    13	whichever conductor ran observed. Neither says what the other says: a
    14	turn, a tool call and a measurement are spans and only spans, and what the
    15	lifecycle carries about them is the one summary fact a reader of a single
    16	simulation asks for — how many turns it reached. Both go through one
    17	reporter, so they are delivered in the order they happened and the
    18	terminal document is last.
    19	
    20	The executor is deliberately a seam. Today it runs each simulation as one
    21	asyncio task in this process; a process- or container-per-simulation
    22	executor implements the same handful of methods and the claim loop never
    23	learns the difference.
    24	
    25	Nothing here may take the whole service down. A control plane that is slow,
    26	broken, or answering nonsense is an ordinary Tuesday, and the loops below
    27	are written so that the worst it costs is the work in flight — never the
    28	simulator itself, and never a capacity slot that no longer comes back.
    29	"""
    30	
    31	from __future__ import annotations
    32	
    33	import asyncio
    34	import contextlib
    35	import logging
    36	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
    37	from typing import Protocol
    38	
    39	from .blob import BlobStore, FilesystemBlobStore, S3BlobStore
    40	from .client import ClaimFailure, ControlPlaneClient, HeartbeatFailure
    41	from .config import MediaSettings, SimulatorConfig
    42	from .contract import ContractViolation
    43	from .model import build_model_client
    44	from .persona import Persona
    45	from .pipeline import Assembled, assemble
    46	from .platform_logging import log_event, simulation_log_context
    47	from .plugs import failed_ending, plug_for
    48	from .redaction import SecretRegistry
    49	from .reporting import Reporter
    50	from .spans import SpanEmitter, trace_id_for
    51	from .spec import SimulationSpec
    52	from .speech import SpeechProviders
    53	from .walk import Conducted, WalkControls, conduct
    54	
    55	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    56	
    57	CLAIM_RETRY_SECONDS = 1.0
    58	
    59	REPEATED_CLAIM_FAILURE_SECONDS = 60.0
    60	"""How often a claim failure that has not changed says so again.
    61	
    62	A control plane that is down fails the same way every retry for as long as
    63	it lasts. Written out each time that is one sentence a second — megabytes
    64	a day of a log nobody can read, with the only thing that would be news, the
    65	failure changing, buried inside it. So a failure speaks up when it is new
    66	and once a minute while it persists; the repeats are still there at DEBUG
    67	for whoever wants to count them."""

    70	def blob_store_for(config: SimulatorConfig) -> BlobStore:
    71	    """Where this simulator's recordings go, decided once at startup.
    72	
    73	    Naming an object-storage endpoint is the whole of what selects it —
    74	    the same shape as naming a media backend, and the reason the entire
    75	    test suite runs against a directory with no container anywhere. The
    76	    two are exclusive because the configuration made them so: a
    77	    deployment with a store has no blob directory to fall back to. One
    78	    place or the other, never both — a copy kept on the container's own
    79	    disk beside the one in the store would hide exactly the fault the
    80	    store is here to fix, until the day a second simulator made half the
    81	    recordings unreadable and nothing said so.
    82	
    83	    Everything above this line is given a :class:`BlobStore` and never
    84	    learns which one it got.
    85	
    86	    The settings are taken apart here rather than handed over whole, so
    87	    that ``blob.py`` stays a leaf: it knows what an object store needs and
    88	    nothing about where a deployment's answers come from. That is what
    89	    lets the seam be tested with five arguments and no environment, and
    90	    what would otherwise make the store's tests configuration's tests too.
    91	    """
    92	    store = config.object_store
    93	    if store is None:
    94	        return FilesystemBlobStore(config.blob_dir)
    95	    return S3BlobStore(
    96	        endpoint=store.endpoint,
    97	        bucket=store.bucket,
    98	        access_key_id=store.access_key_id,
    99	        secret_access_key=store.secret_access_key,
   100	        region=store.region,
   101	    )

   104	class Executor(Protocol):
   105	    """The seam between claiming work and running it.
   106	
   107	    ``free_capacity`` is what the next claim declares; ``submit`` accepts a
   108	    spec and returns without waiting for it; ``wait_for_room`` parks the
   109	    claim loop while the executor is full; ``cancel_all`` and ``drain`` are
   110	    teardown. An executor that runs simulations in processes or containers
   111	    implements this same surface and nothing above it changes.
   112	    """
   113	
   114	    @property
   115	    def free_capacity(self) -> int: ...
   116	
   117	    def submit(self, spec: SimulationSpec) -> None: ...
   118	
   119	    async def wait_for_room(self) -> None: ...
   120	
   121	    def cancel_all(self) -> None: ...
   122	
   123	    async def drain(self) -> None: ...
   124	
   125	
   126	class AsyncioExecutor:
   127	    """Runs each simulation as one asyncio task inside this process.
   128	
   129	    The first executor, and the simplest thing that honors the seam: a
   130	    testing platform's failure domain is forgiving, and per-simulation
   131	    containers would tax exactly the self-hosted deployment where adoption
   132	    lives. Heavier executors can replace this without touching the loop.
   133	    """
   134	
   135	    def __init__(
   136	        self, capacity: int, *, start: Callable[[SimulationSpec], Awaitable[None]]
   137	    ) -> None:
   138	        self._capacity = capacity
   139	        self._start = start
   140	        self._running: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
   141	        self._room = asyncio.Event()
   142	        self._room.set()
   143	
   144	    @property
   145	    def free_capacity(self) -> int:
   146	        return self._capacity - len(self._running)
   147	
   148	    def submit(self, spec: SimulationSpec) -> None:
   149	        if self.free_capacity < 1:
   150	            raise RuntimeError("submit called with no free capacity")
   151	        task = asyncio.create_task(
   152	            self._start(spec), name=f"simulation:{spec.simulation_id}"
   153	        )
   154	        self._running.add(task)
   155	        task.add_done_callback(self._finished)
   156	        if self.free_capacity < 1:
   157	            self._room.clear()
   158	
   159	    def _finished(self, task: asyncio.Task) -> None:
   160	        self._running.discard(task)
   161	        self._room.set()
   162	        if not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is not None:
   163	            simulation_id = task.get_name().removeprefix("simulation:")
   164	            fault = task.exception()
   165	            assert fault is not None
   166	            log_event(
   167	                logger,
   168	                logging.ERROR,
   169	                "egma.simulation.finished",
   170	                "simulation task died before it could report",
   171	                attributes={
   172	                    "egma.simulation_id": simulation_id,
   173	                    "egma.outcome": "failed",
   174	                    "error.type": type(fault).__name__,
   175	                },
   176	                exc_info=fault,
   177	            )
   178	
   179	    async def wait_for_room(self) -> None:
   180	        await self._room.wait()
   181	
   182	    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
   183	        for task in list(self._running):
   184	            task.cancel()
   185	
   186	    async def drain(self) -> None:
   187	        while self._running:
   188	            await asyncio.gather(*list(self._running), return_exceptions=True)
   189

   191	class RunningSimulation:
   192	    """One claimed spec being conducted, and its heartbeat.
   193	
   194	    It is also the one place that sees everything a conductor observes,
   195	    which is why the conversation's spans are authored here rather than
   196	    deeper in. There are two conductors and they observe in two
   197	    currencies: the walk sees a turn at the moment it happened, and the
   198	    voice conductor sees both ends of one, read off the audio. Both report
   199	    to the callbacks below, and what comes out is one emitter for chat and
   200	    voice alike.
   201	    """
   202	
   203	    def __init__(
   204	        self,
   205	        spec: SimulationSpec,
   206	        *,
   207	        client: ControlPlaneClient,
   208	        config: SimulatorConfig,
   209	        secrets: SecretRegistry,
   210	        blobs: BlobStore,
   211	    ) -> None:
   212	        self.simulation_id = spec.simulation_id
   213	        self._spec = spec
   214	        self._client = client
   215	        self._config = config
   216	        self._secrets = secrets
   217	        self._blobs = blobs
   218	        self._reporter = Reporter(
   219	            client,
   220	            spec.simulation_id,
   221	            config.wal_dir,
   222	            delivery_deadline_seconds=config.report_deadline_seconds,
   223	        )
   224	        # The conversation's own record, authored here and delivered by the
   225	        # reporter — the same log, the same ordered sender. Which is what
   226	        # puts every span ahead of the terminal document rather than
   227	        # alongside it.
   228	        self._spans = SpanEmitter(spec.simulation_id, flush=self._reporter.spans)
   229	        self._controls = WalkControls()
   230	        self._first_human_at: float | None = None
   231	        self._first_latency_reported = False
   232	        self._assembled: Assembled | None = None
   233	
   234	    async def run(self) -> None:
   235	        """Conduct to a terminal report, whatever happens on the way."""
   236	        heartbeat = asyncio.create_task(
   237	            self._heartbeat_forever(),
   238	            name=f"heartbeat:{self.simulation_id}",
   239	        )
   240	        try:
   241	            await self._conduct_and_report()
   242	        finally:
   243	            heartbeat.cancel()
   244	            try:
   245	                await heartbeat
   246	            except asyncio.CancelledError:
   247	                pass
   248	            except Exception:
   249	                # The beat is already over and its own loop logged why.
   250	                # Raising here would skip closing the reporter, which is
   251	                # what gets the terminal event onto the wire.
   252	                logger.exception("the heartbeat for %s ended badly", self.simulation_id)
   253	            try:
   254	                await self._reporter.close()
   255	            finally:
   256	                # A failed final SDK-to-WAL handoff must not leave the
   257	                # process-wide provider holding this simulation's route.
   258	                self._spans.abort()
   259	
   260	    async def _conduct_and_report(self) -> None:
   261	        reporter = self._reporter
   262	        reporter.running()
   263	        self._spans.opened()
   264	        log_event(
   265	            logger,
   266	            logging.INFO,
   267	            "egma.simulation.started",
   268	            "simulation started",
   269	        )
   270	        try:
   271	            # The model first, because the pipeline below holds things that
   272	            # have to be given back and only conducting gives them back.
   273	            model = build_model_client(self._spec)
   274	            # One pipeline per simulation, built from its own spec: the
   275	            # plug that knows the connection type, and — for voice — the speech
   276	            # legs around it, selected by this work order's models block.
   277	            # Assembling also decides which of the two conductors this
   278	            # simulation gets. It is validation, so a connection config
   279	            # the plug does not understand is an honest failure rather
   280	            # than a crash.
   281	            assembled = assemble(
   282	                self._spec,
   283	                blobs=self._blobs,
   284	                # The pinned persona version is the only model and voice
   285	                # source. The current direct keys arrived on this claim.
   286	                speech=SpeechProviders.from_models(
   287	                    self._spec.models, vad=self._config.vad_provider
   288	                ),
   289	                media=MediaSettings.for_simulation(
   290	                    self._config.media, self._spec.platform.carrier
   291	                ),
   292	            )
   293	            self._assembled = assembled
   294	            persona = Persona(
   295	                traits=self._spec.persona_traits,
   296	                scenario_instructions=self._spec.scenario_instructions,
   297	                model=model,
   298	            )
   299	            try:
   300	                # Which of the two conductors this simulation gets was
   301	                # decided by assembly, from the spec alone. Both answer
   302	                # the same `Conducted`, so nothing below this line knows
   303	                # which one ran.
   304	                if assembled.conductor is not None:
   305	                    conducted = await assembled.conductor.conduct(
   306	                        persona=persona,
   307	                        max_turns=self._spec.limits.max_turns,
   308	                        max_duration_seconds=(self._spec.limits.max_duration_seconds),
   309	                        controls=self._controls,
   310	                        name=f"sim:{self.simulation_id}",
   311	                        on_utterance=self._on_utterance,
   312	                        on_measured=self._on_measured,
   313	                        on_answered=self._on_answered,
   314	                    )
   315	                else:
   316	                    assert assembled.plug is not None
   317	                    conducted = await conduct(
   318	                        persona=persona,
   319	                        plug=assembled.plug,
   320	                        max_turns=self._spec.limits.max_turns,
   321	                        max_duration_seconds=(self._spec.limits.max_duration_seconds),
   322	                        on_turn=self._on_turn,
   323	                        on_timing=self._on_timing,
   324	                        on_tool_call=self._on_tool_call,
   325	                        on_answered=self._on_answered,
   326	                        controls=self._controls,
   327	                        name=f"sim:{self.simulation_id}",
   328	                    )
   329	            finally:

   104	class Executor(Protocol):
   105	    """The seam between claiming work and running it.
   106	
   107	    ``free_capacity`` is what the next claim declares; ``submit`` accepts a
   108	    spec and returns without waiting for it; ``wait_for_room`` parks the
   109	    claim loop while the executor is full; ``cancel_all`` and ``drain`` are
   110	    teardown. An executor that runs simulations in processes or containers
   111	    implements this same surface and nothing above it changes.

   113	
   114	    @property
   115	    def free_capacity(self) -> int: ...
   116	
   117	    def submit(self, spec: SimulationSpec) -> None: ...
   118

   126	class AsyncioExecutor:
   127	    """Runs each simulation as one asyncio task inside this process.
   128	
   129	    The first executor, and the simplest thing that honors the seam: a
   130	    testing platform's failure domain is forgiving, and per-simulation
   131	    containers would tax exactly the self-hosted deployment where adoption
   132	    lives. Heavier executors can replace this without touching the loop.

   134	
   135	    def __init__(
   136	        self, capacity: int, *, start: Callable[[SimulationSpec], Awaitable[None]]
   137	    ) -> None:
   138	        self._capacity = capacity
   139	        self._start = start
   140	        self._running: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
   141	        self._room = asyncio.Event()
   142	        self._room.set()
   143	
   144	    @property
   145	    def free_capacity(self) -> int:
   146	        return self._capacity - len(self._running)
   147	
   148	    def submit(self, spec: SimulationSpec) -> None:
   149	        if self.free_capacity < 1:
   150	            raise RuntimeError("submit called with no free capacity")
   151	        task = asyncio.create_task(
   152	            self._start(spec), name=f"simulation:{spec.simulation_id}"
   153	        )
   154	        self._running.add(task)
   155	        task.add_done_callback(self._finished)
   156	        if self.free_capacity < 1:
   157	            self._room.clear()
   158	
   159	    def _finished(self, task: asyncio.Task) -> None:
   160	        self._running.discard(task)
   161	        self._room.set()
   162	        if not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is not None:
   163	            simulation_id = task.get_name().removeprefix("simulation:")
   164	            fault = task.exception()
   165	            assert fault is not None
   166	            log_event(
   167	                logger,
   168	                logging.ERROR,
   169	                "egma.simulation.finished",
   170	                "simulation task died before it could report",
   171	                attributes={
   172	                    "egma.simulation_id": simulation_id,
   173	                    "egma.outcome": "failed",
   174	                    "error.type": type(fault).__name__,
   175	                },
   176	                exc_info=fault,
   177	            )
   178	
   179	    async def wait_for_room(self) -> None:
   180	        await self._room.wait()
   181	
   182	    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
   183	        for task in list(self._running):
   184	            task.cancel()
   185	
   186	    async def drain(self) -> None:
   187	        while self._running:
   188	            await asyncio.gather(*list(self._running), return_exceptions=True)

1	"""The conversation, authored as OpenTelemetry spans.
     2	
     3	One ``SpanEmitter`` serves one simulation. Everything a conductor
     4	observes — each turn with who said it and what was said, each tool call
     5	the platform reported, each measurement — becomes a span, stamped when it
     6	happened and handed to a flush as an ordinary OTLP export document. On the wire that
     7	document is what any exporter would send, which is the whole point of
     8	speaking OTLP: a simulation arrives at the same ingest door a customer's
     9	agent posts to, and is the same shape at rest.
    10	
    11	What the platform and this emitter agree on is written down once, in
    12	``packages/simulation-contract/span-vocabulary.md``, and pinned as golden
    13	fixtures beside it: the scope, the span names, the attribute keys, and how
    14	a batch names the simulation it is evidence of. Nothing here may drift
    15	from that document without the fixtures failing on both sides.
    16	
    17	**Delivery is not this module's business.** A flush hands the document to
    18	whoever built the emitter, and the reporter puts it through the same
    19	write-ahead log and the same single ordered sender the lifecycle documents
    20	ride — which is what makes a resend byte-identical and puts every span on
    21	the wire before the terminal document leaves. That ordering is the whole
    22	design: when the control plane records a terminal transition, the evidence
    23	is already stored.
    24	
    25	Two things follow from that and shape everything below.
    26	
    27	**OpenTelemetry authors the record.** The process-wide SDK mints every span id,
    28	tracks parents, and serializes the export. Its one identity adapter gives a
    29	parentless simulation root the trace id already derived from the simulation id,
    30	so the simulation, conversation, and grades can find each other without a
    31	mapping. A retry replays the already-serialized bytes; conducting the same
    32	conversation again creates new span ids and therefore new evidence.

    34	**Timestamps say when the thing happened**, never when it was sent. A
    35	timing span is named for the measure it takes and its own duration *is*
    36	the number, so it is opened one measurement before the moment it was
    37	taken. A turn is opened for as long as it was spoken — one instant on
    38	chat, where a message has no duration, and ear to ear on voice. Two turns

    46	both ends before it says anything, because it read them off the audio

     4	observes — each turn with who said it and what was said, each tool call
     5	the platform reported, each measurement — becomes a span, stamped when it
     6	happened and handed to a flush as an ordinary OTLP export document. On the wire that
     7	document is what any exporter would send, which is the whole point of
     8	speaking OTLP: a simulation arrives at the same ingest door a customer's
     9	agent posts to, and is the same shape at rest.

    12	``packages/simulation-contract/span-vocabulary.md``, and pinned as golden
    13	fixtures beside it: the scope, the span names, the attribute keys, and how
    14	a batch names the simulation it is evidence of. Nothing here may drift
    15	from that document without the fixtures failing on both sides.
    16

    18	whoever built the emitter, and the reporter puts it through the same
    19	write-ahead log and the same single ordered sender the lifecycle documents
    20	ride — which is what makes a resend byte-identical and puts every span on
    21	the wire before the terminal document leaves. That ordering is the whole
    22	design: when the control plane records a terminal transition, the evidence
    23	is already stored.

    28	tracks parents, and serializes the export. Its one identity adapter gives a
    29	parentless simulation root the trace id already derived from the simulation id,
    30	so the simulation, conversation, and grades can find each other without a
    31	mapping. A retry replays the already-serialized bytes; conducting the same
    32	conversation again creates new span ids and therefore new evidence.

    35	timing span is named for the measure it takes and its own duration *is*
    36	the number, so it is opened one measurement before the moment it was
    37	taken. A turn is opened for as long as it was spoken — one instant on

1	"""One simulation walks one exchange: persona and plug, turn by turn.
     2	
     3	The walk is the plug-blind, model-blind middle: it opens the exchange
     4	through the plug, lets the persona and the agent alternate, records every
     5	turn as it flows, measures each answer, and names how it all ended. Four
     6	deliberate endings — the persona concluding, the agent ending, the turn
     7	limit, the duration limit — plus the cancel directive; each is reported
     8	distinctly, and a limit ending is never the agent failing.
     9	
    10	Two hands may stop a running walk from outside its own loop: a cancel
    11	directive honored at a heartbeat, and the duration watchdog. Both act
    12	through :class:`WalkControls`, and the first cause to land is the one the
    13	record shows — a cause arriving after the walk already ended changes
    14	nothing, because what happened is the record.
    15	"""

    20	import contextlib
    21	import logging

    39	It carries nothing, because it is not an observation: it is the boundary
    40	between one answer and the next, and turn-taking is the only thing that
    41	knows where that falls. An answer that produced no words is still an
    42	answer that ended, which is exactly the case a reader of the turns alone
    43	would miss. An agent that speaks first has finished saying its piece the
    44	same way, so the opening counts as one.

   444	    def __init__(self, *, persona: Persona) -> None:
   445	        super().__init__(
   446	            settings=LLMSettings(
   447	                model=persona.model_name,

   464	    @traced_llm
   465	    async def _process_context(self, context: LLMContext) -> None:
   466	        self._reply = None
   467	        self._failure = None
   468	        messages = cast(list[dict[str, str]], context.get_messages())
   469	        reply = await self._persona.reply_to(messages)
   470	        self._reply = reply
   471	        await self.push_frame(LLMTextFrame(reply.text))

   473	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   474	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   475	        if isinstance(frame, LLMContextFrame):
   476	            await self.push_frame(LLMFullResponseStartFrame())
   477	            try:
   478	                await self._process_context(frame.context)
   479	            except Exception as fault:
   480	                self._failure = fault
   481	                await self.push_error(
   482	                    "the persona model could not answer", exception=fault
   483	                )
   484	            finally:
   485	                await self.push_frame(LLMFullResponseEndFrame())
   486	            return
   487	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)

   489	    def take_reply(self) -> PersonaReply:
   490	        """The reply whose native end frame just reached the gate."""
   491	        failure, self._failure = self._failure, None
   492	        reply, self._reply = self._reply, None
   493	        if failure is not None:
   494	            raise failure
   495	        if reply is None:
   496	            raise RuntimeError("Pipecat ended a persona response with no reply")

   501	    """Hold model chunks until Egma applies conclusion and speaking timing."""
   502	
   503	    def __init__(
   504	        self, *, service: _PersonaLLMService, conductor: VoiceConductor
   505	    ) -> None:
   506	        super().__init__()
   507	        self._service = service
   508	        self._conductor = conductor
   509	        self._waiting: asyncio.Future[None] | None = None
   510	        self._due: MediaPosition | None = None
   511	        self._collecting = False
   512	        self._text: list[str] = []
   513	
   514	    async def request(
   515	        self,
   516	        messages: list[dict[str, str]],
   517	        due: MediaPosition,
   518	        push: Callable[[Frame], Awaitable[None]],
   519	    ) -> None:
   520	        if self._waiting is not None:
   521	            raise RuntimeError("the persona model already has a reply in flight")
   522	        waiting = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
   523	        self._waiting = waiting
   524	        self._due = due
   525	        try:
   526	            context = LLMContext(messages=cast(Any, messages))
   527	            await push(LLMContextFrame(context=context))
   528	            await waiting
   529	        except BaseException:
   530	            if self._waiting is waiting:
   531	                self._reset()
   532	            raise

   534	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   535	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   536	        if direction != FrameDirection.DOWNSTREAM or self._waiting is None:
   537	            await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   538	            return
   539	        if isinstance(frame, LLMFullResponseStartFrame):
   540	            self._collecting = True
   541	            self._text = []
   542	            return
   543	        if self._collecting and isinstance(frame, LLMTextFrame):
   544	            self._text.append(frame.text)
   545	            return
   546	        if self._collecting and isinstance(frame, LLMFullResponseEndFrame):
   547	            await self._finish_reply()
   548	            return
   549	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)

   551	    async def _finish_reply(self) -> None:
   552	        waiting = self._waiting
   553	        due = self._due
   554	        assert waiting is not None
   555	        assert due is not None
   556	        try:
   557	            reply = self._service.take_reply()
   558	            received = "".join(self._text)
   559	            if received != reply.text:
   560	                raise RuntimeError(
   561	                    "Pipecat's persona response did not match its model reply"
   562	                )
   563	            if not self._conductor.is_ending:
   564	                await self._conductor.wait_until(due)
   565	                if not self._conductor.is_ending:
   566	                    self._conductor.persona_will_speak(
   567	                        reply.text, concludes=reply.concluded
   568	                    )
   569	                    await self.push_frame(LLMFullResponseStartFrame())
   570	                    await self.push_frame(TextFrame(reply.text))
   571	                    await self.push_frame(LLMFullResponseEndFrame())
   572	        except asyncio.CancelledError:
   573	            waiting.cancel()
   574	            raise
   575	        except Exception as fault:
   576	            waiting.set_exception(fault)
   577	        else:
   578	            waiting.set_result(None)
   579	        finally:
   580	            self._reset()

   584	        self._due = None
   585	        self._collecting = False
   586	        self._text = []

1700	/**
  1701	 * The conversation is underway: `claimed → running`, stamped with the moment
  1702	 * it started, by the claimant conducting it. `undefined` on anything else —
  1703	 * the guarded update is the check, so there is no window in which the row
  1704	 * moves between being looked at and being moved.
  1705	 *
  1706	 * In a transaction because the move and its event are one fact: a guarded
  1707	 * update that matched nothing writes neither, and one that matched writes both.
  1708	 */
  1709	export async function startSimulation(
  1710	  auth: AuthContext,
  1711	  id: string,
  1712	  claimant: string,
  1713	): Promise<Simulation | undefined> {

  1719	      .update(simulation)
  1720	      .set({ status: "running", startedAt: now, heartbeatAt: now })
  1721	      .where(
  1722	        within(
  1723	          auth,
  1724	          simulation,
  1725	          and(
  1726	            eq(simulation.id, id),
  1727	            eq(simulation.claimedBy, validClaimant(claimant)),

  1730	          ),
  1731	        ),

  1744	/**
  1745	 * How every simulation lands: one guarded update — this claimant's row, in a
  1746	 * state the landing may leave, within the caller's reach — writing the
  1747	 * terminal facts, and the run finalized in the same transaction when the
  1748	 * landing was its last. The three landings below differ only in what they
  1749	 * write and what they require, so that is all they say; `undefined` still
  1750	 * means there was nothing here to move.
  1751	 *
  1752	 * The events go in beside them: the conversation landing, and then the run
  1753	 * itself when this landing was the one that finished it.
  1754	 */
  1755	async function landSimulation(
  1756	  auth: AuthContext,

  1758	  claimant: string,

  1763	     * `ended_at`, when the report carried the conduction's own moment; the
  1764	     * stamp below is only the fallback for a report that brought none.
  1765	     */
  1766	    readonly write: Record<string, unknown>;

  1768	    readonly onlyWhere?: SQL | undefined;

    77	def contract_pairs(kind: str) -> tuple[ModelPair, ...]:
    78	    schema = selection_schema(kind)
    79	    provider_schema = schema["properties"]["provider"]
    80	    if "const" in provider_schema:

    91	        if validator.is_valid(example_selection(schema, provider=provider, model=model))
    92	    )
    93	    assert {provider for provider, _model in pairs} == set(providers)
    94	    assert len(pairs) == len(providers)

---
name: graphify
description: "Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools."
---

# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory (HTML viz; add --obsidian for a vault)
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
/graphify <path> --update                             # incremental - re-extract only new/changed files
/graphify <path> --directed                            # build directed graph (preserves edge direction: source→target)
/graphify <path> --whisper-model medium                # use a larger Whisper model for better transcription accuracy
/graphify <path> --cluster-only                       # rerun clustering on existing graph
/graphify <path> --no-viz                             # skip visualization, just report + JSON
/graphify <path> --html                               # (HTML is generated by default - this flag is a no-op)
/graphify <path> --svg                                # also export graph.svg (embeds in Notion, GitHub)
/graphify <path> --graphml                            # export graph.graphml (Gephi, yEd)
/graphify <path> --neo4j                              # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for Neo4j
/graphify <path> --neo4j-push bolt://localhost:7687   # push directly to Neo4j
/graphify <path> --falkordb                           # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --falkordb-push falkordb://localhost:6379   # push directly to FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
/graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)
/graphify <path> --wiki                               # build agent-crawlable wiki (index.md + one article per community)
/graphify <path> --obsidian --obsidian-dir ~/vaults/my-project  # write vault to custom path (e.g. existing vault)
/graphify add <url>                                   # fetch URL, save to ./raw, update graph
/graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it
/graphify add <url> --contributor "Name"              # tag who added it to the corpus
/graphify query "<question>"                          # BFS traversal - broad context
/graphify query "<question>" --dfs                    # DFS - trace a specific path
/graphify query "<question>" --budget 1500            # cap answer at N tokens
/graphify path "AuthModule" "Database"                # shortest path between two concepts
/graphify explain "SwinTransformer"                   # plain-language explanation of a node
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## What You Must Do When Invoked

If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

**Fast path — existing graph:** Before doing anything else, check whether `graphify-out/graph.json` exists. The expected location is `graphify-out/graph.json` relative to the **current working directory** (i.e. the project root where you are running commands). If it exists AND the user's request is a natural-language question about the codebase (e.g. "How does X work?", "What calls Y?", "Trace the data flow through Z") and NOT an explicit rebuild command (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, or a bare path/URL that implies fresh extraction): **skip Steps 1–5 entirely and jump straight to `## For /graphify query`.** Run `graphify query "<question>"` immediately. Do not run detect. Do not check corpus size. Do not ask the user to narrow. The graph is already built — use it.

If no path was given, use `.` (current directory). Do not ask the user for a path.

If the path argument starts with `https://github.com/` or `http://github.com/`, treat it as a GitHub URL - run Step 0 before anything else, then continue with the resolved local path.

Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

### Step 0 - GitHub repos and multi-path merge (only if a URL or several paths)

Only when the path is one or more `https://github.com/...` URLs, or several local subfolders to merge. See `references/github-and-merge.md` for the clone, cross-repo merge, and monorepo flow, then continue with the resolved local path. A plain local path skips this step.

### Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed

```bash
# Detect the correct Python interpreter (handles uv tool, pipx, venv, system installs)
PYTHON=""
GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)
# 1. uv tool installs — most reliable on modern Mac/Linux
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _UV_PY=$(uv tool run --from graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
fi
# 2. Read shebang from graphify binary (pipx and direct pip installs)
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && [ -n "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" ]; then
    _SHEBANG=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
    case "$_SHEBANG" in
        *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) ;;
        *) "$_SHEBANG" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null && PYTHON="$_SHEBANG" ;;
    esac
fi
# 3. Fall back to python3
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then PYTHON="python3"; fi
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null; then
    if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy -q 2>&1 | tail -3
        _UV_PY=$(uv tool run --from graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
    else
        "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q 2>/dev/null \
          || "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages 2>&1 | tail -3
    fi
fi
# Write interpreter path for all subsequent steps (persists across invocations)
mkdir -p graphify-out
"$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)"
# Save scan root so `graphify update` (no args) knows where to look next time
echo "$(cd INPUT_PATH && pwd)" > graphify-out/.graphify_root
```

If the import succeeds, print nothing and move straight to Step 2.

**In every subsequent bash block, replace `python3` with `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)` to use the correct interpreter.**

### Step 2 - Detect files

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import json
from graphify.detect import detect
from pathlib import Path
result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
" > graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json
```

Replace INPUT_PATH with the actual path the user provided. Do NOT cat or print the JSON - read it silently and present a clean summary instead:

```
Corpus: X files · ~Y words
  code:     N files (.py .ts .go ...)
  docs:     N files (.md .txt ...)
  papers:   N files (.pdf ...)
  images:   N files
  video:    N files (.mp4 .mp3 ...)
```

Omit any category with 0 files from the summary.

Then act on it:
- If `total_files` is 0: stop with "No supported files found in [path]."
- If `skipped_sensitive` is non-empty: report the count and list the skipped file names, so a wrongly-flagged source or doc is visible and can be renamed or moved (#2106).
- If `total_words` > 2,000,000 OR `total_files` > 500: show the warning. Then compute the top 5 first-level subdirectories by file count:
  - Read `scan_root` from the detect JSON (always an absolute path to the resolved INPUT_PATH).
  - Concatenate all file lists across all types (`code`, `document`, `paper`, `image`, `video`).
  - Filter out any path that starts with `scan_root + "/graphify-out/"` to exclude converted sidecars.
  - For each file, strip the `scan_root` prefix and take the first path component. Files directly in `scan_root` with no subdirectory count as `(root)`.
  - If all files are in `(root)` with no subdirectories, do not ask to narrow — no subfolders exist. Instead suggest `--no-cluster` to skip the expensive clustering step and proceed.
  - Otherwise rank by count, show the top 5 with file counts, then ask which subfolder to run on. Wait for the user's answer before proceeding.
- Otherwise: proceed directly to Step 2.5 if video files were detected, or Step 3 if not.

### Step 2.5 - Video and audio (only if video files detected)

Skip this step entirely if `detect` returned zero `video` files. When the corpus has video or audio, see `references/transcribe.md` to transcribe them to text first, then treat the transcripts as doc files in Step 3.

### Step 3 - Extract entities and relationships

**Before starting:** note whether `--mode deep` was given. You must pass `DEEP_MODE=true` to every subagent in Step B2 if it was. Track this from the original invocation - do not lose it.

This step has two parts: **structural extraction** (deterministic, free) and **semantic extraction** (LLM, costs tokens).

> **graphify needs no API key. Never ask the user for one, and never block on one.** Code is extracted structurally (AST) with no LLM and no key at all — a code-only corpus (the common `/graphify .` on a repo) skips semantic extraction entirely, so it needs nothing here: go straight to Part A and skip Part B. Semantic extraction (only for docs, papers, and images) uses Gemini **only if** `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` is already set; otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM. graphify does **not** read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or any other provider key. If you catch yourself about to prompt for, wait on, or stop because of a missing API key, that is a misread of this skill — proceed without one.

**Before semantic extraction:** check whether `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is set. If neither is set, print this one-liner to the user:
> Tip: set `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` to use Gemini for semantic extraction (`pip install 'graphifyy[gemini]'`).

Print it once, then continue — do not wait for the user to supply a key. If `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` IS set, use `graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="gemini")` for semantic extraction instead of dispatching subagents. The default Gemini model is `gemini-3-flash-preview`; set `GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL` or pass `--model` in headless CLI flows to override it.

> **No other API keys are read.** When `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` are unset, semantic extraction falls to the host agent itself — the running session is the LLM. On a host that dispatches subagents (e.g. Claude Code), dispatch them as written in Part B. from graphify.detect import save_manifest

# Save manifest for --update

extract = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
# In --update mode, 'all_files' carries the full corpus; 'files' is the changed
# subset. Full-rebuild mode populates only 'files', so the fallback handles that.
# root= relativizes the manifest keys to the scan root (same base as the build),
# so the on-disk manifest is portable across clones/machines and a later --update
# matches cached files instead of missing every one (#1417).
#
# Only stamp semantic files (docs/papers/images) that ACTUALLY produced output:
# a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the
# next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost
# forever (#2015). This mirrors the library extract path exactly
# (cli._stamped_manifest_files + clear_semantic + scan_corpus); do not stamp the
# raw corpus. Code files are always stamped (AST is deterministic); only semantic
# types are gated on output.
from graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files
_corpus = detect.get('all_files') or detect['files']
_manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path('INPUT_PATH'))
# Files dispatched this run (the changed subset) but NOT stamped above still carry
# a stale semantic_hash from a prior run; clear it so detect_incremental re-queues
# them instead of reading them as unchanged (#1948).
_sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')
_dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}
_stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}
_cleared = _dispatched - _stamped
# scan_corpus = the RAW full corpus (not the stamp-filtered subset) so in-root
# files newly excluded since last run are dropped rather than masquerading as
# deletions; untouched files' prior rows are still preserved (#1908).
_scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}
save_manifest(_manifest_files, root='INPUT_PATH', scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)

# Update cumulative cost tracker

output_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)

cost['total_output_tokens'] += output_tok

## Interpreter guard for subcommands

Before running any subcommand below (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, `query`, `path`, `explain`, `add`), check that `.graphify_python` exists. If it's missing (e.g. user deleted `graphify-out/`), re-resolve the interpreter first:

```bash
if [ ! -f graphify-out/.graphify_python ]; then
    GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" ]; then
        PYTHON=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
        case "$PYTHON" in *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) PYTHON="python3" ;; esac
    else
        PYTHON="python3"
    fi
    mkdir -p graphify-out
    "$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)"
fi
```

## For --update and --cluster-only

Both are non-default subcommands. `--update` re-extracts only new or changed files; `--cluster-only` reruns clustering on the existing graph. See `references/update.md` for both flows.

## For /graphify query

When `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists and the user asks a question about the corpus, answer from the graph rather than rebuilding it:

```bash
graphify query "<question>"

Before traversal, expand the question against the graph's own vocabulary so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise. If the `graphify query` CLI is unavailable, fall back to an inline NetworkX traversal of `graphify-out/graph.json`. Answer using only what the graph output contains, and quote `source_location` when citing a specific fact. For that vocab-expansion step, the BFS/DFS traversal modes, the `--budget` cap, the NetworkX fallback, `save-result` feedback, and the `/graphify path` and `/graphify explain` flows, see `references/query.md`.

Neither is part of the default build. When the user runs `/graphify add <url>` to fetch a URL into the corpus, or passes `--watch` to auto-rebuild on file changes, see `references/add-watch.md`.

When the user asks to install the post-commit auto-rebuild hook or wire graphify into a project's CLAUDE.md, see `references/hooks.md`.

- Never invent an edge. If unsure, use AMBIGUOUS.
- Never skip the corpus check warning.
- Always show token cost in the report.
- Never hide cohesion scores behind symbols - show the raw number.
- Never run HTML viz on a graph with more than 5,000 nodes without warning the user.

    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22	
    23	**The scripted codec.** Scripted speech is real PCM — 16-bit signed
    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which
    30	channel.
    31	
    32	The tones stay under 3 kHz so that the narrowest band a connection can
    33	carry, 8 kHz telephony, still holds them.

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   226

   230	
   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())
   277	        await self.push_frame(
   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )
   284	        await self.push_frame(TTSStoppedFrame())

   286	
   287	class ScriptedSTT(SegmentedSTTService):
   288	    """What the agent said, read back out of the audio it arrived as.
   289	
   290	    Segmented rather than streaming, because that is what this leg
   291	    honestly is: it reads a whole stretch of speech at once. A full-duplex
   292	    line hands its pipeline one small slice of audio at a time and never a
   293	    turn, so a leg that transcribed each slice on its own would read every
   294	    utterance as a string of fragments. The base class here is the one a
   295	    local model subclasses: it buffers between the voice detector's start
   296	    and stop and calls :meth:`run_stt` once with the whole utterance.
   297	    """
   298	
   299	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   300	        super().__init__(
   301	            sample_rate=None,
   302	            settings=STTSettings(model=None, language=None),
   303	            ttfs_p99_latency=1.0,
   304	        )
   305	
   306	    @property
   307	    def wants_wav_segments(self) -> bool:
   308	        """Raw PCM, not a WAV file: the codec reads samples, not headers."""
   309	        return False
   310	
   311	    def can_generate_metrics(self) -> bool:
   312	        return False
   313	
   314	    @traced_stt
   315	    async def run_stt(self, audio: bytes) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame | None, None]:
   316	        yield TranscriptionFrame(
   317	            text=decode_speech(audio, self.sample_rate),
   318	            user_id="",
   319	            timestamp=time_now_iso8601(),
   320	        )

   322	
   323	class ScriptedVAD(VADAnalyzer):
   324	    """Hears the scripted codec exactly, and nothing else.
   325	
   326	    A voice activity detector answers one question — is somebody speaking
   327	    in this window of audio — and the scripted codec answers it without a
   328	    model: a tone is loud and quiet is exactly zero samples. So this leg
   329	    reads the samples and says so, which makes every speech boundary it
   330	    reports a sample position rather than a probability.
   331	
   332	    That exactness is what the record rests on. A window is one encoded
   333	    byte wide, so a scripted utterance begins and ends on a window
   334	    boundary at every band; the detector confirms speech one window in and
   335	    silence :data:`QUIET_WINDOWS` windows later, and both are corrected
   336	    back by exactly those windows — so the interval it hands over is the
   337	    interval that was really spoken, to the sample.
   338	
   339	    Silero is the leg a live simulation hears with; see :func:`build_vad`.
   340	    """
   341	
   342	    SPEAKING_WINDOWS = 1
   343	    """How many windows of speech confirm that somebody started talking."""
   344	
   345	    QUIET_WINDOWS = 4
   346	    """How many windows of silence confirm that they stopped. Long enough
   347	    to sit through a gap between words, short enough that the persona is
   348	    not left waiting on somebody who has finished."""
   349	
   350	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   351	        self._window_samples = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE
   352	        super().__init__(
   353	            sample_rate=None,
   354	            params=VADParams(
   355	                confidence=0.5,
   356	                # Loudness is already the whole of this leg's answer, so a
   357	                # second loudness gate could only disagree with it.
   358	                min_volume=0.0,
   359	                start_secs=0.0,
   360	                stop_secs=0.0,
   361	            ),
   362	        )
   363	
   364	    def set_sample_rate(self, sample_rate: int) -> None:
   365	        """Learn the input rate from Pipecat's start frame."""
   366	        self.params.start_secs = (
   367	            self.SPEAKING_WINDOWS * self._window_samples / sample_rate
   368	        )
   369	        self.params.stop_secs = self.QUIET_WINDOWS * self._window_samples / sample_rate
   370	        super().set_sample_rate(sample_rate)
   371	
   372	    def num_frames_required(self) -> int:
   373	        return self._window_samples
   374	
   375	    def voice_confidence(self, buffer: bytes) -> float:
   376	        return 1.0 if carries_speech(buffer) else 0.0

   103	    raw = _text(name)
   104	    if raw is None:
   105	        return fallback

   108	    except ValueError:

   112	def _seconds(name: str, fallback: float, *, allow_zero: bool = False) -> float:
   113	    """A duration from the environment, refused rather than guessed at."""
   114	    raw = _text(name)
   115	    if raw is None:
   116	        return fallback
   117	    try:
   118	        value = float(raw)
   119	    except ValueError:
   120	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a number of seconds, got {raw!r}") from None
   121	    if not math.isfinite(value):
   122	        # `float()` reads "nan", "inf" and "-inf", and the range check
   123	        # below cannot catch the first two: every comparison against nan
   124	        # is False, and +inf is greater than zero, so both would be taken
   125	        # as a duration. What they would then buy is silence — an
   126	        # infinite heartbeat interval never beats again, so the control
   127	        # plane sees an orphan while the simulation is conducting fine,
   128	        # and an infinite report deadline retries one report until the
   129	        # process ends, holding a capacity slot nothing will free. Both
   130	        # are worse than not starting.
   131	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a finite number of seconds, got {raw!r}")
   132	    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
   133	        wanted = "zero or more" if allow_zero else "more than zero"
   134	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be {wanted}, got {raw}")
   135	    return value

   161	def _writable_directory(name: str, path: Path) -> Path:
   162	    """A directory the simulator can really write to, proven at startup.
   163	
   164	    In a compose deployment both directories are a mounted volume, and a
   165	    volume that is read-only, or owned by somebody else, or shadowed by a
   166	    file, does not announce itself. It waits — for the recording at the
   167	    end of a voice exchange, or for the first report on its way out — and
   168	    then takes that simulation down with it. A container that cannot keep
   169	    what it is asked to keep should say so before it claims anything.
   170	
   171	    Proving it is also making it, which is the other half of the point: a
   172	    fresh volume arrives empty and nothing else would create the two
   173	    directories inside it.
   174	    """
   175	    try:
   176	        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   177	        probe = path / f".egma-simulator-write-probe-{os.getpid()}"
   178	        probe.write_bytes(b"")
   179	        probe.unlink()
   180	    except OSError as refusal:
   181	        raise ValueError(
   182	            f"{name}={path} is not a directory the simulator can write to: {refusal}"
   183	        ) from refusal
   184	    return path

    78	
    79	A line is never digitally silent — it carries comfort noise, and a
    80	threshold is what tells that apart from speech. Set low enough to hear a
    81	quiet talker and high enough to ignore a line's own hiss.

    83	
    84	TONE_BASE_HZ = 200
    85	TONE_STEP_HZ = 10
    86	TONE_AMPLITUDE = 8000
    87	
    88	CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE = (0.6, 1.5)
    89	"""What the cartesia mouth accepts as a speed multiplier, its own numbers.
    90	
    91	A speed outside this range is refused. The adapter never changes the value
